articleTitle: Workspace Exploration and Kinematic Design of a 6-DOF Dual-Arm Robotic System
abstract: Dual-arm manipulation systems hold the potential to revolutionize complex industrial and defense applications by enabling coordinated, human-like hand actions. This paper presents an in-depth workspace analysis of dual-arm manipulation using MATLAB, with a focus on visualizing and analyzing the collaborative workspace between two UR5e robotic arms. The Denavit-Hartenberg (DH) parameters for each arm are identified to accurately model their kinematic structures, and the forward kinematic solutions are derived to guide motion planning. Additionally, the collaborative workspace is computed and visualized using a Monte Carlo method, providing a probabilistic approach to assess reachability and interaction zones between the two arms. The results highlight the significance of workspace overlap and collision avoidance on task efficiency and precision. This study offers valuable insights into optimizing dual-arm systems for complex, coordinated tasks, with a particular emphasis on space utilization and coordinated control strategies across various applications.

articleTitle: Crowd Density Estimation and Real-time Monitoring using Digital Twins in Transportation Hubs
abstract: Digital twins transcend static models, offering dynamic virtual replicas of physical entities, thereby revolutionizing data-driven decision-making across industries. This paper proposes a novel digital twin system specifically designed for real-time crowd management, leveraging object detection with YOLOv8s architecture and 3D plotting using a three.js library. Our proposed system can be used as an edge analytics tool to minimize latency and enhance real-time decision-making, crucial for applications like autonomous vehicles, industrial automation, and large crowd gatherings. The proposed system was implemented and tested on multiple pre-recorded video feeds and it was evaluated based on time to process frames. For the proposed system an accuracy of 84.21% was achieved by comparing the actual number of people present in the given frame vs the number of people detected. This research demonstrates that digital twin models provide a robust, proactive approach to optimizing operations, enhancing safety, and increasing visitor satisfaction in crowded spaces.

articleTitle: Design and Operational Principles of Mobile GIS: A Practitioner’s Perspective
abstract: Mobile GIS is the integration of Mobile and GIS technology to manage geospatial operation and data from mobile or hand-held computing platforms. This is primarily helpful in field data collection and location-based services. The rapid growth in modern mobile systems further helped the transition of geospatial technology from a desktop environment to field settings. The GIS domain has gradually evolved from a Desktop-based stand-alone environment to a web-based Distributed environment, thereby paving the road for web GIS and mobile GIS. The Desktop GIS allows the user to carry out different rich and computationally heavy geospatial tasks within the office environment. It depends on a desktop-based computing infrastructure. Enterprise GIS or Web GIS is the web-based technique to access geospatial operations through internet browsers. This makes it possible to store, integrate, and analyze enterprise data along with geospatial information.Mobile GIS facilitates geospatial operations in the real field environment beyond desktop environment. It makes field data collection easy and enables real-time updates of ground data in the centralized GIS server. Thus, the GIS database has always up-to-date information that can be used across various applications. The current paper looks into various aspects of the design and development principles of a mobile GIS. The concept and challenges of a mobile GIS are revisited and explored. This is an industrial concept paper that discusses the details of the architectural design of a mobile GIS.

articleTitle: A Software Architectural Model for Generative Artificial Intelligence with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen AI) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) are cutting edge technologies, in the field of AI. This study presents an architectural framework that combines these technologies to improve decision making in systems. Through case studies we explore how integrating AI with RL enhances performance in real world applications. By incorporating RL strategies, our approach ensures parameter settings and successful operation of the AI model leading to results. This framework can be applied in multiple software applications like information synthesis and creative simulation. Despite challenges like training instability and limited resources that generative models face, our research recognises the potential that this approach can effectively addess these issues. Our innovative framework uses RL techniques to improve the models performance during training. The results suggest that combining RL with AI not overcomes existing limitations but also opens up possibilities, for data driven applications. This hybrid method pushes the boundaries of models offering solutions across different fields.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Banking System: Emulating Traditional Banking Operations on Ethereum with Real-Time Interest Accrual and Fixed Deposit Mechanism
abstract: In order to leverage blockchain technology and replicate some of the essential functions of traditional banks, the paper presents a decentralized banking system that is currently operational on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet. Enrollment of users, safe deposit and withdrawal features, instantaneous money transfers, and a sophisticated fixed deposit mechanism with adjustable deadlines are all provided by this system. This project features a significant innovation in its real-time interest accrual function, which lets users earn and withdraw interest continuously with second-by-second rate updates. The decentralized, transparent, and safe nature of this banking experience is guaranteed. With an emphasis on how this system might upend established banking models, the paper addresses the system’s design, implementation, and performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Skill Recommendation System and Resume Analysis using AI
abstract: The goal of the Skill Recommendation System and Resume Analysis is to improve resume writing skills and raise the probability of getting hired for a job. It offers specific guidance on how to make your CV stand out from the thousands of other applicants on internet job sites. The system generates tailored recommendations for course selection and skill improvement based on information it has extracted from resumes, including experience and talents. The suggested method aims to help job seekers improve their resumes and speed up the hiring process. The technology extracts relevant data from resumes using natural language processing (NLP) techniques and offers specific recommendations for course selection and improvement of skills. The aim of the system is to help companies find qualified applicants more quickly and help job seekers improve their resumes by automating the resume analysis process.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Build Detection and Classification of Tomato Leaf Diseases Using Advanced CNN Architectures
abstract: Tomato leaf diseases pose a crucial threat to agricultural productivity, making the development of effective and accurate detection methods crucial. To address these challenges, our project utilizes deep learning for automated disease detection. By leveraging advanced feature extraction techniques, we eliminate the require for manual feature engineering and segmentation. A custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) developed for multi-class classification. The model involve of four convolutional layers with increasing filter sizes (32, 64, 128, and 256), utilizing ReLU and SELU activations for capable feature extraction. Max-pooling layers are employed to bring down the spatial dimensions of the data, followed by a fully connected layer with 1024 units. The final softmax layer classifies inputs into three distinct categories. The network is improved using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.0001 and trained with sparse categorical cross-entropy loss. The proposed model attained an accuracy of 94%, evidencing its effectiveness in classifying image data while maintaining a stabilty between computational efficiency and carrying out, offering a highly exact method for identifying tomato leaf infection.

articleTitle: Sensor Signal Malicious Data Binary Classification: A Comparison of QNN, and VQC
abstract: The importance of cyber security postures in various information technology (IT) or operations technology (OT) environments cannot be overstated, considering the significance of the cyber-physical system. The escalating risks in the intricate realm of cyberspace must be immediately evaluated, given their potential to inflict significant harm. Although machine learning has made significant progress to date, it is crucial to acknowledge that future cyberattacks will likely become more sophisticated. In this context, quantum machine learning is a clear and logical choice for the future. However, are available resources ideally open-source sufficient enough for finding a trade-off between the accuracy and computation time is a curious query worth contemplating. Size of the dataset is also another factor to include in the wondering space. This research aims to evaluate and compare several quantum supervised classification techniques with a conventional traditional method for binary classification of a dataset containing harmful sensor data.

articleTitle: Hybrid Image Compression Using DCT and Autoencoder
abstract: Medical image processing is an emerging area that has an effect on recognition, analysis and treatment techniques of the diseases. In medical image processing compression is required to reduce the bandwidth and storage related issues. In this method DCT and Autoencoder based image compression technique is used for the better compression of the medical brain images. To get the separate Region of Interest(ROI) and non-ROI based region Otsu method is considered. DCT and Autoencoder based hybrid compression is achieved on ROI and non-ROI regions of an image respectively. The evaluation parameter of this method are Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structure Similarity Index matrix (SSIM), Feature Similarity Index Matrix (FSIM), Compression Ratio (CR) and Space saving(SS) percentage. For the medical brain images proposed method has PSNR of 44.45db, SSIM of 0.97, FSIM of 0.99, CR 9.26 and SS of 89.9(%).

articleTitle: A study on Post Quantum- Recent Techniques, Challenges and Bibliometric analysis
abstract: The advent of quantum computers spells doom for classical encryption schemes. Asymmetric key cryptosystems are easily solved by quantum computers using Shor’s algorithm and Grover’s algorithm in polynomial time compared to exponential time for classical brute forcing techniques. Therefore, current encryption schemes are easily decrypted by quantum computing technologies. This indicates a paradigm shift in the field of cryptography and necessitates the development of quantum resistant algorithms. Therefore, the field of post-quantum cryptography is vital to protect sensitive data, which includes grave matters of national security. Thus, this work highlights the need of accelerating the impactful research on quantum resistant cryptosystems along with a bibliometric study showcasing present research output. Moreover, throws light on the state-of-the-art quantum resistant algorithms along with their methodologies and challenges (in particular, the NIST finalists) and suggests future work needed to safeguard matters of public safety and national security.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power System Dynamics with Renewable Integration and Battery Storage for a 3 bus ring connected system
abstract: Energy from renewable sources like wind and solar is unpredictable and subject to weather-related supply fluctuations and system instability. Grid management requires accurate renewable energy output forecasts, but errors might produce mismatches. The significant challenge is that, utilities must enhance forecasting methods for accurate resource allocation and renewable output prediction. In this paper, a 3 bus ring system developed with a pandapower library is proposed by emphasizing the dynamic interaction between generation with renewable energy, consumption, and storage, showcasing how advanced battery management can enhance grid stability and efficiency. Plots are used to illustrate the computation of net power surplus or deficit, the use of excess power to charge the battery without exceeding capacity, and the discharge of the battery to satisfy load demand without going below safe charge.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Software Framework for Multi-axis Robotic Systems Using ROS 2 and EtherCAT
abstract: Multi-axis robotic systems demand high bandwidth and rapid control frequency updates for their effective operation. These systems are designed with distributed controller allowing sensor, control computation, and actuator nodes to communicate via network. In these systems, the high-level software controller handles tasks such as motion planning and control built on top of low-level control systems resulting in jitter and latencies introduced by software and communication components. The timing issues affect control, stability, and error correction capabilities ultimately degrading system performance and therefore, precise timing is essential for effective operation of control algorithms, particularly while computing state variables such as position, velocity, torque etc. The objective of this work is to investigate the impact of timing inaccuracies and to propose practical solution by integrating ROS 2 with EtherCAT. EtherCAT’s high bandwidth capability effectively manages the control of numerous joints, while ROS 2, with its Data Distribution Service (DDS) middleware, enhances real-time capabilities. To ensure the real-time capabilities of the ROS 2 communication stack and EtherCAT, a complete end-to-end ROS 2 managed node lifecycle pipeline has been implemented and real-time experiments are performed with PREEMPT_RT Linux on a motion control test setup to demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Comparison of Path Planning Algorithms for Indoor Static Environment
abstract: Indoor path planning application area involves cleaning, surveying, inspection & mobile robotics etc. In this paper, we performed a comparative analysis of number of well-known algorithms for indoor environments, to find the best algorithm providing the shortest path & execution time. The obstacle space was simulated using a 2D environment created using a binary grid map of 200x200 cells, which represents indoor environment features like walls, narrow passages, closed rooms, door openings, etc. Popular methods for path planning include visibility graphs, grid-based methods, sampling-based methods, virtual potential fields, etc. Each of these methods is suitable for a certain environment. Complete path planners like visibility graphs are mathematically complex & impractical for many real systems. Grid-based planners like A* or wavefront planners are easy to implement but are suitable for low-dimensional configuration space. Planners that rely on sampling such as Rapidly-exploring random tree (RRT) & Probabilistic roadmap (PRM) are computationally less expensive than grid-based planners & rely on a random function to choose a sample from configuration space to find obstacle-free space & a simple local planner to connect these samples to move towards a goal. We have selected a variety of algorithms, each representing different path planning criteria involving simple bug behavior, sampling-based planners, distance cost function with a heuristic approach & compared the final results to find a suitable algorithm for the indoor environment. It was observed that sampling based & heuristic-based distance function planner performs best among selected algorithms for the indoor environment under consideration.

articleTitle: Implementation of Deep Learning Techniques for Deepfake Classification: A comparative study using ResNet-50 and VGG16
abstract: This work investigates the use and assessment of ResNet-50 and VGG16 deep learning models for detecting deepfake images using the Labelled Faces in the Wild (LFW) dataset. The methodology encompassed thorough preparation of the dataset and the utilisation of both models to differentiate between authentic and altered facial photos. The models' performance was evaluated using fundamental criteria including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. VGG16 demonstrated superior performance compared to ResNet-50, achieving an accuracy of 93.87%, recall of 96.23%, and an F1 score of 94.41%, while ResNet-50 achieved a precision of 92.54%, recall of 95.26%, and F1 score of 93.88%. Although both models achieved good accuracy, VGG16 had superior stability and generalization across the whole dataset. The study determines that VGG16 is the more dependable model for detecting deepfakes on the LFW dataset. It suggests that future efforts should concentrate on enhancing ResNet-50 or creating ensemble methods to enhance detection capabilities.

articleTitle: From Pixels to Perception: Adversarial Camouflage Patterns Designed to Evade Detection Models and Human Observation
abstract: Camouflage techniques can effectively evade detection and tracking systems that rely on human visual perception or optical sensors during aerial reconnaissance of military targets. While the advent of deep neural network-based object detection models has enabled the identification of even well-camouflaged targets, these models are vulnerable to adversarial examples. Adding perturbations to camouflage patterns can attack the detection models, but this deteriorates the appearance of the camouflage and can be easily recognized by human vision. The purpose of this paper is to develop adversarial camouflage patterns that not only undermine object detection models but also deceive human perception. The research methodology involves synthesizing camouflage patterns for varied terrain environments using image processing techniques and feeding them into a custom GAN framework to create deceptive adversarial camouflage patterns. The experimental results demonstrate that the generated adversarial camouflage patterns can effectively fool both state-of-the-art object detection models and human observers, showcasing the effectiveness of the proposed approach over traditional camouflage designs.

articleTitle: Early Identification of Nutritional Gaps in Pregnant Women Using Nail Images for Healthcare Analysis
abstract: During pregnancy, the mother needs to care for her nutritional deficiencies as it may cause severe health issues for both the mother and her baby. The two most important nutrients are calcium and iron, and their deficiencies can prevalently cause anaemia, premature birth, depression, neurological disorders, weakened bones, slow growth, and osteoporosis which compromises the overall well-being of the mother and her baby. Traditional methods to diagnose these deficiencies are through blood tests done in laboratories. These tests are invasive, costly, and sometimes inaccessible. This paper proposes a novel approach to detect calcium and iron deficiencies in pregnant women using deep learning-based nail analysis and a comprehensive questionnaire, in pregnant women, ultimately contributing to improved maternal and fetal health outcomes. An appropriate deep-learning model was selected for the given problem statement. The model architecture consisted of convolutional layers, pooling layers, and dense layers. The model was trained on the prepared dataset to accurately classify nail images into healthy, calcium-deficient, and iron-deficient categories.

articleTitle: Exploring the scope of Blockchain-based Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs) in Crowdfunding Platforms
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative crowdfunding platform utilizing Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) to tackle the challenges linked to conventional payment methods and the regulatory limitations of earlier cryptocurrency-based solutions. We present a practical prototype, demonstrating the feasibility of the CBDC approach. An extensive evaluation comparing CBDCs with Ethereum and traditional systems confirms its superior performance. This research marks the initial step toward understanding the potential of CBDCs in crowdfunding, setting the stage for future exploration and innovation in this evolving financial landscape.

articleTitle: A New VMP Approach Based on CPU and Memory Using Bin Packing
abstract: Cloud computing is one of the demanding technologies that provide services with flexibility in terms of pay as per use, access to the module from anywhere, etc. To meet the growing demand from users, cloud providers are developing extensive data centers. The core technology behind cloud computing is virtualization, which delivers computing services through virtual machines (VMs). In the dynamic cloud computing environment, numerous users request various services, making it essential to implement efficient resource allocation policies to meet user demands. The goal is to maximize resource utilization while minimizing energy consumption by optimizing the use of physical server resources. Simulations conducted using the CloudSim simulator demonstrate that this approach maximizes resource utilization by selecting the minimum number of hosts. The algorithm treats the three parameters as dimensions in a 3D bin packing (BP) model, with the workloads for the data center generated from PlanetLab leftovers. In a scenario with 50 VMs and 40 hosts, the proposed algorithm reduces energy consumption from 0.98 kWh to 0.38 kWh, which shows a significant improvement. The novelty of this paper is the development of a dynamic bin-packing algorithm that optimizes both resource utilization and energy consumption by efficiently managing virtual machine placement in cloud data centers

articleTitle: TwitAnalyze: A Deep Dive into Twitter Profile and Comment Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Twitter is a platform where millions of users voice their opinions and sentiments on various topics on a daily basis. In this digital landscape, businesses recognize the importance of validating their online reputation, using customer opinions to maximize profits. This project specifically focuses on gathering data, evaluating it, and extracting public and private opinions. The key aspect of the analysis is the implementation of vectorization through a pipeline which enables the sentiment classification of new tweets. It explores the significance of opinion mining in shaping online reputation and business strategies. Through rigorous machine learning model evaluation, the study seeks to provide insights into sentiment analysis methodologies and their real-world applications.

articleTitle: Simplifying Customer Interaction with an Integrated Chatbot Solutions for Restaurants
abstract: The main innovation behind this paper is a new chatbot solution for health and diet promotion in restaurants. Developed with advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and AI technologies, the chatbot simplifies communication between diners and restaurant services resulting in major improvements for customer satisfaction. Although restaurants chatbots still need more improvement in terms of broader scope toward people with a bit health consciousness diet, current studies reveal the ability to leverage this tool for better operational andcustomer experience. All in all, this chatbot is distinguished by recommending menus that are personalized to the dietary preferences and restrictions of its customers so as to ensure they are given options when it comes down to their health where a meal plan can be applied. In addition, the chatbot supplies detailed nutritional data over every menu item to make it easier for customers when making healthier choices. Packed with these essential features, the chatbot enhances the overall dining experience for users and boosts health awareness in restaurants. This focused service is an example of howAI can create a healthier food space for diners.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Hidden Patterns: AI-Driven Morphological and Compositional Analysis of Antimony Sulpho-telluride Thin Films Synthesized via Arrested Precipitation Technique
abstract: Antimony sulpho-telluride (Sb2(S1-x, Tex)3) thin films hold immense potential for optoelectronic applications. However, a comprehensive understanding of their morphology and chemical composition is crucial for optimizing device performance. This study aims to address this knowledge gap by investigating the structural and compositional properties of these films. To achieve this, antimony sulpho-telluride thin films were synthesized on glass substrates using the arrested precipitation technique. The morphological characteristics of the as-deposited films were analyzed through X-ray diffraction (XRD). To precisely figure out the chemical makeup, a combination of methods was used for the first time on binary or ternary metal chalcogenide thin films. These methods includedEnergy Dispersive X-ray micro-analysis (EDAX), Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS), and Extractive Spectrophotometry (ESP). The results obtained from these techniques reveal the correct stoichiometry of the synthesized films. Notably, the V/VI ratio increases with selenium content, indicating an increase in anti-site defects. These results highlight how crucial it is to carefully control the composition to adjust the light and electronic properties of antimony sulpho-telluride thin films. This study lays the foundation for future research aimed at optimizing these materials for specific device applications.

articleTitle: Detection Of Malignant Cancerous Nuclei Using Quantum Hadamard Edge Detection Algorithm
abstract: Cancer is a hazardous ailment, becoming even more ominous due to its capacity to remain unnoticed. The significance of cancer research lies in its role in enhancing both the detection and treatment of this disease, ultimately leading to improved quality of life for affected individuals. The process of edge detection assumes a pivotal role in image processing, as it aids in the identification of object boundaries within images. In recent years, quantum computing has garnered substantial attention for its potential to address complex problems more efficiently than classical computers. In this work, we employed edge-detection technique to annotate images related to breast cancer. We have attempted the portion of cancerous nuclei in one biopsy data sample with several malignant nuclei and validated these findings through manual examination. We have used Quantum Hadamard Edge Detection Algorithm (QHED) to identify the nuclei edges. We implemented the algorithm on quantum simulator platforms ie qiskit and Amazon Web Services (AWS). We present the results from implementation on 4 qubits in AWS simulators i.e. State Vector (SV) Simulator and Density Matrix (DM) Simulator. In qiskit implementation, the algorithm was implemented on 4096 x 4096 pixels of biopsy image, that required 24 qubits in the qiskit platform when performing on a CPU. Further, the research presented herein compares the outcomes of Canny edge detection and the results achieved through quantum edge detection from real data and we observe that the results from the quantum approach are at par with the results obtained from the classical approach.

articleTitle: Investigation of Non-linear Optical Properties of CdSe Quantum Dots by Z-Scan Technique
abstract: Cadmium Selenide (CdSe) quantum dots were produced using a chemical colloidal synthesis technique. Their nonlinear optical behavior was evaluated through the Z-scan experiment, where closed-aperture measurements revealed self-defocusing effects, and open-aperture measurements indicated saturable absorption. The quantum dots were extensively characterized using UV-Vis spectroscopy, photoluminescence analysis, and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. These findings highlight the potential applications of CdSe quantum dots in the use of optical switching and photonic technologies.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Enhanced IoT System for Real-Time Identification of Ayurvedic Raw Materials
abstract: The aim of this study is to design an innovative system that leverages on-chip Internet of Things (IoT) and deep learning technologies for the identification of Ayurvedic raw materials. The system employs an ESP32-CAM module that possesses on-chip processing capabilities to immediately capture high-quality photos on the device, therefore addressing crucial concerns regarding the validity and quality of these materials. These photos are analyzed using robust on-chip deep learning algorithms that were trained on a large dataset of 4,500 photos from 15 different classifications. To increase the accuracy of their input material classification, the models use advanced preprocessing approaches to extract important aspects including form, color, and texture. This method ensures the precise identification of resources, which not only encourages sustainable harvesting techniques but also guarantees the quality and safety of Ayurvedic goods. This approach greatly increases the efficacy and dependability of Ayurvedic therapies by fusing innovative technology with conventional medical procedures. This has a huge positive impact on both practitioners and patients.

articleTitle: LoRaWAN Security Framework to Mitigate DoS Attacks at the Gateway Level using Machine Learning
abstract: LoRaWAN, a popular protocol for low power wide area networks, is mainly used in Internet-of-Things oriented applications because of its ability to communicate over long distances and energy efficiency. Nonetheless, the security measures of the protocol have been discovered to be susceptible to different forms of attacks like eavesdropping, replay, flooding, jamming and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. This study offers a thorough examination of security concerns and evaluates current remedies. In addition, we suggest a new method to reduce DoS attack by implementing machine learning approach to enhance the security of LoRaWAN networks.

articleTitle: Advanced Drone Navigation and Landing with Multi-Algorithm Integration for Parrot MiniDrone
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive navigation algorithm for autonomous line following and precision landing using a Parrot MiniDrone. The system leverages multiple parallel-running image processing algorithms, each contributing to different aspects of the drone’s navigation. The Dynamic Crown Pursuit Algorithm (DCPA) generates target points to guide the drone along a predefined line, while the Slope-Based Speed Control Algorithm optimizes speed during turns and Off-Track Algorithm corrects deviations to maintain the drone’s position. Additionally, an End Marker Detection algorithm enables precise landing within a designated area. These algorithms are integrated into a Stateflow model that governs the drone’s behavior across various flight stages, including takeoff, line following, alignment, turning, and landing. The landing process is executed in three stages to ensure accuracy and speed. The proposed system was tested in a simulated environment, demonstrating its effectiveness in maintaining accurate line following and executing precise landings. To further validate the system’s overall performance, a comparative analysis with existing methods was conducted, revealing the superior speed and precision of the proposed approach. This makes it well-suited for autonomous drone missions that require high precision and speed in navigation and landing, with potential applications in fields such as surveillance, inspection, and delivery services.

articleTitle: Transforming Insurance Processes with ICP Blockchain Integration
abstract: The conventional insurance sector is widely recognized for its inefficiencies, exorbitant costs, and restricted accessibility. The integration of Internet Computer Protocol (ICP) and blockchain technology presents a revolutionary shift in the management of insurance processes. This paper explores the transformative potential of ICP in automating and decentralizing key insurance operations such as underwriting, policy management, and claims processing. By leveraging the MotoKo framework, an innovative decentralized insurance platform, we propose an architecture that utilizes smart contracts, decentralized oracles, and automated governance to increase transparency, reduce operational costs, and enhance accessibility. ICP's high-speed transaction processing capabilities and scalability provide a robust infrastructure for global insurance solutions, removing the need for traditional intermediaries and ensuring data security.

articleTitle: Wideband Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Defected Ground for 5G,6G, and mmWave Application
abstract: Rectangular dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) with multiple frequency band operations and high gain are the proposed design. The X, K, Ka and Ku bands are among the frequency ranges it covers. The antenna features a microstrip feed and two strategically placed circular and rectangular incisions on its Defected Ground Structure (DGS) to enhance performance. These design elements increase bandwidth, regulate current distribution, and improve impedance matching, making the antenna more suitable for high-frequency applications. the suggested antenna performs at the operating frequencies 10.9GHz,14.9GHz,22.2GHz,27.6GHz and 34.4GHz ,its S11 =31.67dB,S11=16.07dB,S11=18.78dB, S11=32.4dB and S11=20.16dB and covering a bandwidth of 10.13-11.72GHz ,13.83-16.21GHz, 18.32-23.05GHz and 32.91-44.02GHz respectively, where good impedance matching is evident. It cover a bandwidth of 14.67%,15.97%,21.26% and 26.56% respectively. A gain of 6.36dB at 10.9GHz,5.57dB at 14.9GHz,6.06dB at 22.2GHz,7.08dB at 27.6GHz and 9.14dB at 34.4GHz radiation efficiency was found to be more than 94.38% within the targeted working frequency spectrum 10.13 to 11.72GHz, more than 94.93% within the targeted working frequency spectrum of 13.83GHz-16.21GHz, more than 96.39% within the targeted working frequency spectrum of 18.32GHz-23.05GHz, more than 98.6% within the targeted working frequency spectrum of 26.3GHz-32.46GHz and more than 99.4% within the targeted working frequency spectrum of 32.91GHz-44.02GHz. Applications where dependable, high-performance operation is crucial, like satellite communications, military aircraft, defense tracking systems, medical, and radar communication systems, are particularly well-suited for this antenna.

articleTitle: Equity Research Chatbot Using LLM: A Responsive Agent for Investment Research
abstract: Our research paper includes the combination of chatbot development and research on various companies' fundamentals (P&L, Balance sheet, and Cash Flow) for giving end users precise investment advice.The literature on technologies like machine learning (ML), neural networks, and Generative AI in financial analysis is surveyed, emphasizing the growing body of research using Large Language Models (LLMs) and their applications using chatbot assistance for investment opportunities. Additionally, previous studies on chatbots in finance are reviewed to contextualize their role in equity research.The methodology outlines the research approach, data collection method, and usage of LLMs in this study. Here the data used are the pdf files containing company financial reports which are then fed into the chatbot for further processing. The data regarding current market trends and overall fundamental analysis provides a clear idea to chatbot for suggesting precise investments. Here NLP processes include text chunking, building semantics, and knowledge base for proceeding to further steps. Further, our results include categories of questions for which we have also showcased its graph that mentions the response time and accuracy versus the type of question asked to the chatbot. This analysis gives an efficient understanding of the chatbot. Overall, this research contributes to the knowledge of how chatbots can transform equity research, paving the way for more efficient and accessible financial analysis in the digital age.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cognitive Quality Inspection in Manufacturing through Siamese Few-Shot Learning
abstract: Defect detection in manufacturing remains challenging, with traditional methods relying on inflexible, hardcoded image processing techniques. While deep learning approaches show promise, they often lack scalability across product variations and require extensive training data. This paper presents a novel few-shot learning-based strategy for defect detection, addressing these limitations. Our proposed solution centers on a Siamese Defect classification model utilizing the Swin-L (Shifted Window Transformer) architecture. This approach enables efficient scaling across new products with minimal technical overhead. The models are trained on the industry-standard MVTEC dataset and optimized for real-time processing on embedded GPU devices, ensuring practical applicability in manufacturing environments. The developed prototype incorporates automated removal of defective items while preserving detailed information for subsequent analysis. By combining few-shot learning with advanced model architectures, our solution offers a reliable and highly scalable approach to defect detection.

articleTitle: Demand Response and Dynamic Pricing Simulation in a 4-Bus Power System
abstract: This paper proposes a simulation of a 4-bus power system network, inspired by the example in “Power System Analysis” by J.J. Grainger and W.D. Stevenson. The simulation incorporates dynamic pricing, demand response mechanisms, and power flow analysis using Pandapower, an open-source Python library for power systems modeling. The objective of this paper is to demonstrate how dynamic pricing and demand response can interact to balance generation and load in a power grid. By analyzing the effects of dynamic pricing on load profiles and generator outputs, this research aims to contribute to a deeper understanding of demand response strategies and their potential benefits in enhancing grid stability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Explainable AI Model for Medical Insurance Premium Prediction using Ensemble Learning with SHAP Analysis
abstract: Medical insurance premium prediction is a crucial task for both insurers and consumers. This paper presents ensemble-based techniques to predict medical insurance prices effectively. The trained models were evaluated based on various quantitative metrics. Explainable AI using SHAP analysis is carried out for model interpretation. Histogram Gradient Boosting produced training and testing accuracies of 91.06% and 85.28%, respectively. The Random Forest (RF) model achieved training and testing accuracy values of 96.48% and 81.65%, respectively, while the Gradient Boosting (GB) model resulted in training and testing accuracies of 87.68% and 83.84%. Histogram Gradient Boosting (HGB) performed best among the techniques in terms of error metrics, producing mean squared error and root mean squared error measures of 6454819.22 and 2540.63, respectively, which are the lowest among the techniques used. On the other hand, Random Forest (RF) produced the highest mean squared error and root mean squared error values of 8045175.00 and 2836.40, respectively, but had the lowest mean absolute error of 1210.14.

articleTitle: Autonomous Navigation of Humanoid Robots Using Kinect Sensor: A Vision-Based Approach for Real-Time Obstacle Detection and Path Planning
abstract: This research presents a novel perspective for an autonomously navigated humanoid robot system which unifies a Kinect Xbox 360 sensor, and L298N motor drivers with Arduino Uno for harnessing real-time depth sensing and vision-based obstacle detection. The robot can conclusively navigate, avoid obstacles and change the direction of its path if an obstacle is found. The Kinect sensor provides enumerated outer environmental data, allowing for decisive path planning and navigation. Arduino Uno processes the sensor data and sends directive commands to the motors via motor controllers through sequential communication. This paper proposes, and analyzes the navigation system’s performance, and proves its advantages compared to existing models.

articleTitle: Bird Species Classification and Prediction Using Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: The BirdClef-2024 dataset, which includes acoustic recordings of 182 Western Ghats species, was used to classify and predict bird species in this study. Three machine learning algorithms were analyzed for their accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score – K Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM). The Random Forest model outperformed the other models in all metrics. The paper contains sections on dataset composition, preprocessing steps, algorithm implementations as well comparisons of the model’s performances. Such issues have been successfully addressed through advanced pre-processing techniques coupled with complex machine-learning algorithms despite the intricate nature of the sound signals. A Streamlit GUI that is user-friendly has been developed to facilitate real-time recognition of birds by breed; this can contribute to surveillance for environmental biodiversity conservation efforts.

articleTitle: Extracting Valuable Insights from The Handwritten Feedback
abstract: This paper describes the collection and analysis of feedback data which is crucial for evaluating the success of any event and identifying areas of improvement. However, when feedback forms are distributed in paper format, extracting the text responses into a machine-readable format for analysis can be a tedious and error-prone manual process. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) Technology offers an automated solution for digitizing text from scanned documents, but its accuracy can be impacted by various factors like image quality, font styles, and language complexities. This study investigates the use of Gemini 1.5 Pro, a multimodal AI, to extract text data from PDF scans of collected handwritten feedback forms. After evaluation of Gemini’s performance across a range of PDF qualities and comparing its output to manually transcribed data, the results demonstrate Gemini's high accuracy rates, even on lower quality scans, enabling efficient extraction of feedback responses while minimizing manual effort. This solution offers a scalable and reliable approach for educational institutions, professional organizations and other bodies to digitize survey responses for deeper qualitative and quantitative computational techniques.

articleTitle: Iot-Based Smart Dustbin for Waste Level Monitoring and Segregation
abstract: The concept of waste segregation management is being implemented in our daily lives, for dry and wet waste separation. It was being implemented to avoid mixed waste collection. Mixed waste collection leads to poor waste management causing reduced recycling efficiency. At the same time sorting mixed waste requires additional processing, increasing the cost of waste collection. Periodically checking the rubbish bins' level is also necessary to prevent overflow, which can lead to unsanitary conditions in the community and surrounding area. To address all the issues, an Arduino-based Internet of Things system that uses a soil moisture sensor and an ultrasonic sensor with the assistance of a NodeMCU is suggested. Using a servo motor, the soil moisture sensor assists in separating the dry and wet trash into the dustbin. The NodeMCU and ultrasonic sensor with Arduino-based hardware components are used for measuring the level of the dustbin. A notification app has been developed using Blynk to send e-notifications to the authorities when the garbage bin is full. This will facilitate the timely collection of the garbage avoiding unhygienic conditions.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Strengthening Network Intrusion Detection Systems
abstract: Strengthening network security is a must in today's digital landscape. Existing Intrusion Detection Systems commonly make use of deep learning techniques such as Deep Neural Networks to identify malicious & anomaly activities. However, there are serious problems of overfitting and huge demand for computational resources in this system that hinder the efficiency and scalability of this system. It introduces an advanced form of an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) which integrates a hybrid machine learning algorithm with Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) along with other machine learning techniques to improve threat detection. This system would realize the recognition of established patterns as well as new anomalies about attacks by means of enhanced feature engineering and real-time AI-driven threat intelligence. It also addresses scalability for more extensive and complex configurations of the network as well as response mechanisms that automatically neutralize threats quickly. Then there is user behavioral analytics that helps in identifying insider threats. It is aimed at providing an all-embracing security solution that is strong and adaptable, greatly improving overall protection of the network. Hence, the effective execution of this project will thus provide a new benchmark for the effectiveness of IDS in delivering reliable security across different sectors as well as paving the way for further improvements in cybersecurity around the globe.

articleTitle: Transforming Fetal Health Monitoring: Advanced Machine Learning Innovations for Accurate Prognosis
abstract: Early detection of pregnancy-related illnesses, such as congenital heart defects, neural tube defects, Down syndrome, and Inborn Errors of Metabolism (IEM), is vital for ensuring the health of both the fetus and the expectant mother. Leveraging advanced ML techniques-specifically Decision Trees, KNN, and Random Forest-can significantly enhance the accuracy of predicting these conditions. Decision Trees provide a transparent, interpretable model that visualizes decision-making through a series of binary splits, enabling healthcare professionals to understand the rationale behind predictions. In contrast, KNN operates on the principle of proximity, classifying new data points based on the 'k' nearest neighbors in a multidimensional space, making it effective in scenarios with complex, non-linear relationships. Meanwhile, Random Forest improves predictive performance by aggregating the outputs of multiple Decision Trees, thus mitigating overfitting and enhancing reliability. This ensemble approach draws on the diversity of trees, each trained on random subsets of data, allowing it to capture intricate interactions among variables. Together, these ML techniques utilize extensive historical data to autonomously predict pregnancy-related conditions, forming a sophisticated decision support system that complements traditional screening methods. By integrating these advanced algorithms, healthcare providers can achieve more accurate early diagnoses, ultimately improving maternal and fetal health outcomes and paving the way for targeted interventions.

articleTitle: Bit-Serial RISC-V CPU Core
abstract: The 32-bit serial RISC-V CPU is a novel bit-serial CPU core that implements the RISC-V instruction set architecture. Its unique bit-serial Datapath, with an internal data width of only one bit, enables ultra-small and low-power design especially suitable for resource-limited embedded systems and FPGAs. There has been growing interest in using bit-serial over bit-parallel execution in machine learning workloads. This paper explores an 32-bit serial RISC-V CPU architecture in detail: it analyzes its diverse core modules, like the bit-serial ALU, register file interface, control logic, and memory interface. A primary focus is on analyzing the lifecycle of executing instructions on the 32-bit serial RISC-V CPU to demonstrate the difference between executing an instruction on a word-parallel CPU with thousands of wires compared to only 32 wires in a bit-serial RISC-V CPU. Most acute challenges with this approach are complexity and performance trade-offs since one must broadcast and then concatenate wires once to form a full-size processor word. For instance, while single-cycle one-stage instructions, like other ALU operations, require only one 32-cycle phase for their execution, two-icon. In light of recent trends, including the IoT, the growth and impact of sensor nodes and the increasing energy-efficiency focus of tomorrow’s accelerators, we can envision crucial application domains for bit-serial machines such as the 32-bit serial RISC-V CPU that prioritizes silicon area and energy efficiency over performance.

articleTitle: Enhanced Object Detection using YOLOv8: Identifying Vehicles and Pedestrians in Urban Environments
abstract: With the vast usage of cameras and sensors for vehicles and crowd management in smart cities, their detection and tracking are paramount. Traditional cars and pedestrian detection methods have limitations in the motion of objects, accuracy, detection in real-time, etc. This paper uses a Vehicles and Pedestrian detection approach based on the YOLOv8 algorithm, which leverages the advantages of deep networks for real-time object detection and mitigation of false alarms, occlusion handling, and motion blur. The targeting classes such as cars, pedestrians, cyclists, trucks, vans, trams, and people sitting were used for experimentation and validation of the approach. YOLOv8's architecture was deliberately chosen for its optimal balance of speed and accuracy. The paper outlines the dataset preparation, training, and evaluation processes, emphasizing adaptations for diverse conditions. YOLOv8's architecture was deliberately chosen for its optimal balance of speed and accuracy.

articleTitle: Leveraging Transfer Learning: Fine-Tuning methodology for Enhanced Text Classification using BERT
abstract: Text Classification is the most widely studied problem area in Natural Language Processing (NLP). BERT is the most popular NLP model based on Transfer Learning with its pre-trained model being widely used for such tasks. It generates contextualized word/ sentence embeddings by applying "Self-Attention and Feed Forward" mechanism through multiple layers. The [CLS] token is the only token in BERT which captures semantically-relevant context for the complete input sentence. BERT-based language models output [CLS] token embedding which represents the input sentence effectively, however, the need for more efficient and accurate sentence embedding still remains a research area in NLP. This paper is to explore the effectiveness of [CLS] token pooled from intermediate encoder layers of the BERT model using Mean and Max pooling methods on Amazon product review dataset. Results obtained during the experiment clearly shows the superiority of CLS pooling strategies over default [CLS] tokens.

articleTitle: Dual-Stage Amplification of All PM Yb-Doped Ultrafast Fiber Laser Modelocked by SESAM
abstract: In this study, a ytterbium doped ultrafast fiber laser was realized using a real saturable absorber called Semiconductor Saturable Absorber Mirror. The resonator cavity was designed in a linear cavity. Theoretical simulation and experimental realization were done based on the optimized parameters. The output from the stable resonator was fed into dual stage amplification stages, which boosted the average power to ~150 mW.

articleTitle: Enhanced Image Analysis for Detecting Malaria Infection in Blood Samples
abstract: The methods of detecting malaria infected cells from microscopy images are discussed in detail in this paper. Malaria disease being a world health problem today, there is need to develop better diagnosing technique because of the high death rate that has been plunged to this disease. Having used a dataset of 27,558 images as infected and uninfected, this study employs Convolutional Neural Networks(CNN), Fuzzy and VGG19 models for semiautomated classification with higher speeds and accuracies as opposed to other methods. It consists of mandatory phases, which predetermine preparing the data set for training, including resizing, normalization, and data augmentation. Among to feature selection, SelectKBest method is used in order to enhance input features of the model. Initial experiments with the CNN model again revealed high accuracy greater than 90%, thereby confirming the use of the model in real–life diagnosis of malaria. In addition, the study emphasises the importance of feature extraction and the use of machine learning in the diagnosis function. The outcomes support the adoption and use of automated detection techniques as the human factor contributes greatly to errors in diagnosis, practices should embrace such technologies leading to the fight against malaria.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Compressive Strength Prediction of 3D-Printed Biocha-Reinforced PLA Biocomposite
abstract: The study pioneers the employment of biochar-reinforced polylactic acid biocomposites in 3D printing to enhance sustainability in additive manufacturing. This research examines the compressive strength of 3D-printed biochar-reinforced polylactic acid biocomposite with fused deposition modeling (FDM). Also, various machine learning algorithms were employed for building prediction models. The selected process parameters under investigation were the %wt. content of biochar (%BC), layer thickness (LT), infill density (ID), and printing patterns (PP). The mechanical compression test was done in accordance with ASTM D695-15, and Taguchi L16 was used for designing the experiments. Various machine learning algorithms, namely linear regression (LR), support vector machines (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGB), random forest (RF), and artificial neural networks (ANN), were employed for building prediction models. The result of the mechanical test shows that for 1% biochar content at 100% infill density, the maximum compressive strength and compressive strength to weight ratio were 79 MPa and 16494.21 MPa/kg, respectively. The most accurate prediction of compressive strength for the proposed 3D-printed biocomposite was done by the XGB model with a 98% R-squared value, 1.91 MAE, and 2.71 RMSE for the test dataset.

articleTitle: Improved tuning of fractional-order PID controller for an AVR system using geometric mean optimizer
abstract: This paper presents an effective tuning strategy for the Fractional Order Proportional-Integral-Derivative (FOPID) controller that improves the dynamic performance of an automatic voltage regulator (AVR) in power systems. The proposed controller fine-tunes essential design parameters, including proportional, integral, and derivative gains, as well as the integral and derivative orders, using the recently reported Geometric Mean Optimizer (GMO) algorithm. We demonstrate that an integral absolute error (IAE) cost function improves the regulation performance by using time domain analysis. We also conduct robustness studies on the proposed system. Comparative analyses with existing works demonstrate that the proposed FOPID controller achieves competitive performance with the reported techniques.

articleTitle: Performance of FSOC Link Establishment Using Scan/Stare Approach
abstract: The last few decades have seen rapid advances in information and communication technology. The bandwidth and high-capacity requirements due to the increased use of the Internet and broadband services have exceeded our expectations in the twenty-first century. Free space optical communication (FSOC) uses the optical carrier in the near-infrared (IR) and visible bands and is considered a viable solution for realizing very high-speed and large-capacity communication links. It is a line-of-sight communication that uses a laser to transmit the information signal between two transceivers over an unguided channel, which may be either the atmosphere or free space. This technology offers several advantages over conventional Radio Frequency (RF) communication systems, such as high data rates, enhanced data security, absence of multipath fading, and wide bandwidth. It is also license-free. This work explores the possibility of free space optical communication with multiple nodes which can be used for communicating between remote vehicles. Initially, the communication link is established with fixed nodes with the help of an Arduino board for data transmission and reception. Data types transmitted and received are video, message, and text files. We further improved the setup by using Arduinos with a scan/stare approach. We use the same link to demonstrate the file transfer system. We have developed a GUI to transfer any file for communication. Our setup can be utilized in remote data acquisition systems with a secure communication link for shipto-shore communication, surveillance systems, and communication networks near volatile national borders.

articleTitle: Implementation of OOK and PPM Modulation with PRBS and BER for Optical Wireless Communication Using High-Speed FPGA
abstract: With the advancement of society, the need for high-speed communication networks also increases. Optical Communication is one way to achieve high speed and reliable communication. Optical Communication offers a higher bandwidth as compared to RF signals, and the usage of the RF spectrum requires a license whereas Optical communication is free to use. Optical Fiber communication does provide a higher data rate. Still, it is a tedious and expensive task to install and maintain the fiber connection, thus providing a way for optical wireless communication. In this paper, we discuss the implementation of different modulation techniques in Optical Wireless Communication by using a Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) to improve the reliability of the communication link while also obtaining a high data rate. A Pseudo Random Bit Sequence (PRBS) data is generated through the FPGA which is modulated to On-Off Keying (OOK) and Pulse Position Modulation (PPM) modulation, Laser diodes and LEDs are used to transmit the modulated data, and a PIN diode is used to receive the transmitted data, the reliability of the link is measured by calculating the Bit Error Rate (BER).

articleTitle: Deepfake Image Detection Using Yolov8
abstract: Due to growing number of fake media and the possible problems with misinformation and identity theft, deepfake image recognition has become a hot topic. In order to evaluate the efficacy of widely recognized deep learning models in detecting and classifying deepfake images, we compare and contrast YOLO (You Only Look Once) V8, CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), combination of LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) with CNN and ResNet in this paper. The capacity to recognize photos that have been manipulated effectively is essential for maintaining trust regarding digital media and preventing the spread of deceptive data. The objective of our research is to explain each model's abilities, limitations and performance in the context of deepfake image recognition. We evaluated each model's accuracy, precision, and F1-scores using a dataset of 190402 images, half real and half fake that cover a wide spectrum of deep fake images. Based on the evaluation metrics, each model was ranked in terms of its ability to separately describe and determine original versus generated photos with focus on detecting subtle changes eluding human senses. The comparison research shows each model's nuanced capabilities, offering light on the implications for applications in the real world like detecting and controlling the spread of deep fake information across numerous internet platforms. Our findings help towards building deep fake detection systems, further understanding the comparative performance of state of the art deep architectures. This study shall inform more effective deep fake detection systems that can guarantee trust and security in digital media environments. Accuracy achieved by model is 96%, precision score was 94%, recall value is 0.98, F1 score has a value of 0.95.

articleTitle: Blockchain based E-Voting System on Smartphones
abstract: India, the world’s largest democracy, faces significant challenges in conducting free and fair elections due to the prevalence of vote tampering, booth capturing, and rigging. To address and solve these challenges, a blockchain-based e-voting system will be developed that is secure, transparent, and accessible to all eligible voters in India. The decentralized nature of blockchain, combined with the transparency and security of smart contracts written in Solidity, will ensure that the voting process is tamper-proof and transparent. The system will be developed and tested on Ethereum testnet, and the complexity of existing systems will be simplified into a simple smartphone application that can be accessed by all eligible voters in India. The system will remove dependency on crypto wallets like Meta-mask, the backend api’s are developed using node.js, express.js and web3.js. SHA-3 will be used for hashing and encryption purposes. The frontend will be developed using React Native, ensuring a user-friendly and accessible interface. The successful implementation of this blockchain-based e-voting system could revolutionize the democratic process in India, making it more accessible, secure, and transparent, and setting an example for other countries to follow.

articleTitle: Pre-Processing Techniques for Mobile SMS Spam Detection
abstract: This project addresses the challenge of SMS spam through advanced text analysis techniques. Starting with a literature review on current spam detection methods, we aim to develop a robust model using a curated dataset of labelled SMS messages. Our approach includes detailed feature analysis, pre-processing steps for data consistency, and visualization techniques like word clouds to identify common spam indicators. By converting textual data into a machine learning-compatible format with a document-term matrix, our system effectively classifies messages as spam or legitimate, advancing the field of SMS spam detection.

articleTitle: Stable CoM Trajectory Generation for Biped Robots based on Heuristic Capture Point Tracking Approach
abstract: Biped locomotion is a complex phenomenon. As the bipedal robotic system possesses multiple degrees of freedom (DoF), the resulting dynamics is highly nonlinear and coupled. However for practical purposes, reduced and simplified dynamical models such as Linear Inverted Pendulum Model (LIPM) have been widely used for gait generation. In this work, an LIPM based Capture Point (CP) method has been worked out to achieve stable and robust walk for biped robot. An existing algorithm has been modified to avoid infeasibility of solution while generating the desired trajectories of Zero Moment Point (ZMP), CP and Center of Mass (CoM) for stable bipedal locomotion and the efficacy of the approach is validated through simulations. It is shown that the modification also offers an approach to adjust footprint up to a certain extent according to design requirements or terrain conditions.

articleTitle: Blockchain Pervasive Ledger Technology for Healthcare Using Rough Set Theory
abstract: Managing and securing patient data in the healthcare sector is critical. While existing research on integrating blockchain technology with healthcare systems shows promise in enhancing data security and privacy, challenges in data analysis and decision-making accuracy persist. Traditional methods often struggle with imprecise and incomplete data, resulting in unreliable outcomes. This paper proposes a novel framework that integrates blockchain pervasive ledger technology with rough set theory to address these issues. By leveraging the immutable and transparent nature of blockchain and the data analysis capabilities of rough set theory, we aim to improve data security, privacy, and decision-making in healthcare. The proposed framework employs the Apriori algorithm for rule extraction and the Proof of Stake (PoS) consensus mechanism for blockchain transactions. We demonstrate the framework's effectiveness using a real-world dataset from the MIMIC-III (Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care III) database, which includes detailed patient records such as symptoms, test results, diagnoses, and treatment outcomes. The system architecture and mathematical foundations are discussed, along with empirical results showcasing enhanced decision-making accuracy and data security. Our results indicate a significant improvement in data analysis and security, with a 92% accuracy rate in medical diagnoses compared to traditional systems. This research contributes to the development of more reliable and secure healthcare data management systems, ultimately improving patient care and outcomes.

articleTitle: Transparent Diabetes Risk Prediction through Interpretable Machine Learning and XAI Integration
abstract: Diabetes is one of chronic diseases be afflicted to youth all around the world. This study focuses at the use of various machine learning (ML) methods that works better in type-2 diabetes risk prediction. We developed and evaluated various models, including Random forest, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, XGBoost, Bagging with different architectures. The study throw light to importance of model’s transparency and Interpretability with Explainable Artificial Intelligence to gain trust in model. We used PIMA dataset with different sampling and cross validations techniques to propose best model with 86% accuracy and 93% AUC-ROC value. The literature review covers recent advancements in Diabetes predictions, classification, care and managements. The results show that proposed model can significantly enhance Diabetes risk prediction and classification with additional trust and explainabilty to improve transparency in model as compared to traditional black box models.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Smart Exoskeleton for Posture Correction and Mobility Enhancement using Sensor Fusion
abstract: The main focus of this project is to develop a lightweight exoskeleton that provides dynamic support to spine, helps improve posture and enhance mobility. This model is a non-invasive and ergonomic framework which integrates real-time monitoring posture and helps in correction of posture. This model is designed in a way which assures maximum comfort and flexibility in day-to-day activities. It mainly focuses on user comfort and safety. By using the advanced lightweight materials and sensor technologies it ensures the user has a better spinal health and functional movements.

articleTitle: Violence Detection in Surveillance Systems Using MobileNetV2 and Deep Learning
abstract: This paper addresses the critical need for efficient real time violence detection in security systems. Traditional methods often lack the ability to respond promptly and accurately in dynamic environments. To overcome this challenge, we developed a deep learning-based system integrated with cloud technology and instant alert mechanisms. The system utilizes OpenCV for video processing and the MTCNN framework for face detection, leveraging a pre-trained MobileNetv2 model to identify violent content in live video streams. Our model achieved an accuracy of 95.76% with a precision of 94.25%, recall of 93.50% and F1-score of 93.87% in detecting Violent incident upon detection, the system extract key frames, enhances them for clarity, and uploads them to Firebase Storage. Simultaneously, the system gathers the device's geolocation and sends a notification with the image and location to specified Telegram group via bot. Extensive testing demonstrates the system's effectiveness in detecting Violent incidents, providing a reliable tool for enhancing public safety. Future enhancements could focus on expanding its deployment to larger networks, improving detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Enhanced Image Processing and CNN Approaches for Accurate Detection of Wheat Stripe Rust
abstract: Stripe rust, induced by the fungus *Puccinia striiformis f.sp. tritici*, poses a significant risk to wheat fields, dispersing via spores carried by the wind and resulting in broad outbreaks. Proper disease management includes applying fungicide treatments on seeds, fertilizers, and timely sprays, especially if the disease is identified early. Due to the fluctuating timing and location of outbreaks every season, decisions on fungicide application should rely on data from the current season. This research centers on accurately identifying wheat stripe rust disease by utilizing image-processing and deep learning methods. Numerous techniques were assessed, such as transfer learning and different convolutional neural network (CNN) structures. Preprocessing images to eliminate background noise and optimizing the deep learning model with fewer training epochs lead to highly precise classification of wheat diseases, reaching a 97 % accuracy rate on the test set. Types like healthy, septoria, and stripe rust were effectively recognized. The research also examines various advanced methods in image processing and deep learning, offering valuable guidance for future studies. This review is focused on helping researchers discover efficient ways to detect wheat stripe rust, which will help improve disease control.

articleTitle: Real-Time Gesture-to-Speech Conversion System for Mute Person
abstract: This study introduces a machine learning-based system that assists mute individuals by recognizing real time hand gesture using a convolutional neural network (CNN). Captured via a laptop camera, these gestures are converted into text or speech for accessible non-verbal communication. The model is trained on a large dataset, accurately identifies various gestures, such as a raised finger indicating a need for food. A user-friendly camera window dashboard displays real-time results, ensuring practicality for daily use. The system boasts high accuracy and quick response times, making it effective for real-time interactions. Future enhancements may include expanding gesture recognition and improving robustness, advancing assistive technology for better communication.

articleTitle: Design & analysis of Optical Ring Resonator with Circular Cavity as Add-drop Multiplexer
abstract: From the last decade, there has been immense interest in development of optical components. Optical components can be broadly classified into two types viz. active and passive components. These components are used for purpose of splitting, multiplexing, filtering etc. In order to investigate performance of these components, computationally complex Maxwell’s equations are solved either in time or frequency domain. Numerous mathematical methods are developed to solve these equations for analysis of wave propagation inside optical components. The effectiveness of these method depends on the dimensions of the component, wavelength and step size used in the problem. Optical ring resonators are passive components, which are used as channel dropping filters in dense wavelength division multiplexing(DWDM). Filtering performance of ring resonators depends upon various parameters such as size and shape of cavity, coupling length, separation gap from adjacent waveguides etc. In this paper, finite difference beam propagation method(FDBPM) is used to analyze the filtering performance of optical ring resonator with circular cavity. The filtering performance is determined by selecting circular cavities with different diameters and its separation distance for adjacent parallel waveguide. Simulation results shows that maximum optical power can be dropped for circular cavity with smaller diameters with lesser separation gaps, which are consistent with theoretical results. This paper also investigates effect of negative separation gap on filtering performance of ring resonator.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Universal Basic Income System
abstract: This project presents a conceptual design for a decentralized Universal Basic Income (UBI) system implemented on the blockchain. Leveraging smart contracts, the system autonomously distributes regular payments to individuals living below a predefined income threshold, eliminating the need for intermediaries or government intervention. The system allows users to register, update their income status, and receive payments securely through blockchain transactions. While the provided Solidity code offers a basic framework for the UBI system, further development is required to address identity verification, governance, funding mechanisms, and regulatory compliance. Overall, the project lays the foundation for a transparent, efficient, and inclusive UBI solution driven by blockchain technology.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using AI and Machine Learning Models: A Systematic Review for Effective Intervention
abstract: Autism is a brain developmental condition that may impact the everyday life of affected individuals. Toddlers suffering from ASD are labeled by difficulties in social interaction, connecting, lack of eye contact, ignoring danger, preferring to play alone, sensitivity to loud noises, and repetitive behavior compared to normally developed (ND) children. This systematic review examines the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) models for the early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), emphasizing their potential for enabling timely and effective interventions. The significance of this research lies in addressing the critical need for early ASD diagnosis, which can substantially improve outcomes for affected individuals. The novelty of this study is its comprehensive analysis of cutting-edge AI and ML techniques specifically applied to ASD detection, providing insights into their efficacy and limitations. The methodology involved a systematic search of peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2022 across major databases, including PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Scopus. Studies were selected based on predefined inclusion criteria, focusing on AI and ML models used for early ASD detection. Key findings reveal that AI and ML models, particularly deep learning algorithms and ensemble methods, demonstrate promising results in early ASD detection, with some models achieving accuracy rates exceeding 95%. The review identified that behavioral data, neuroimaging, and genetic information are the most commonly used input features for these models. However, challenges persist in terms of model interpretability, dataset bias, and generalizability across diverse populations. This systematic review highlights the potential of AI and ML models as valuable tools for early ASD detection, potentially revolutionizing diagnostic processes and enabling earlier interventions. Future research should focus on developing more robust, interpretable models and validating them across larger, more diverse datasets to enhance their clinical applicability and reliability in real-world settings.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Safety: An Intelligent Drowsiness Detection System Based on Deep Neural Networks
abstract: The aim of this research is to create an intelligent vehicle system that can effectively mitigate the risks associated with drowsy driving, thereby preventing road accidents. Various factors like driver exhaustion, challenging road conditions, and adverse weather contribute to motor vehicle crashes, leading to over 1.35 million deaths annually, as estimated by entities such as the World Health Organization (WHO). To achieve this, the development of a robust warning system is crucial. In this study, we proposed an alert system to detect drowsy drivers. It utilizes a video stream process (VSP) to analyze the gaze's eye-aspect ratio (EAR) and geometric distance through an innate reflex model. Additionally, a facial landmark-based algorithm is employed for accurate eye recognition. When driver drowsiness is detected, the system issues a warning message, along with crash impact and location information, and activates the voice surveillance system. The suggested technique establishes a non-invasive approach for evaluating driver weariness in connection with accident severity. The camera, the fundamental element of this system, continuously acquires facial landmarks recognized by designated locations and analyzes them. Drivers who are distracted and have poor lighting may show signs of sleepiness.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review and Novel Approach for Detection of Zero Day Vulnerabilities
abstract: The research community has placed a greater emphasis on developing a wide, reliable, and effective intrusion detection system (IDS) because of the increasing cyberattacks over the past few decades. Traditional signature-based detection methods are ineffective in finding zero day attacks because the signatures of these attacks are typically not known in advance. Although smart community networks greatly improve people’s comfort and convenience, they also raise security threats by making private information and system weaknesses more accessible to hackers. The issue has gained increased attention due to the rise of zero day attacks, which have the potential to exploit undiscovered vulnerabilities in the intrusion detection system (IDS) to defeat it. A cyberattack that exploits a software vulnerability on the same day that it is made publicly known is referred to as a zero day attack. Because the vulnerability is quickly exploited after discovery, the name "zero day" describes the fact that engineers have no time to address it. Since, zero day attacks take advantage of vulnerabilities that the software vendor is unaware of and has not yet patched, it might be difficult to identify them. This review paper keeps the track of various detection method for Zero Day attack and suggesting novel approaches for zero day attack detection.

articleTitle: Bi-LSTM Model based Person Gender classification using Gait Energy Image and Transfer Learning Techniques
abstract: Several applications have found that human gait provides important motion information. Irises, thumbprints, faces, gait, voice, and many other characteristics are utilized by human recognition AI to identify individuals in a distinctive way. The ever-increasing amount of online image data has created a significant need for Artificial Intelligence (AI) algorithms capable of executing classification tasks such as Gender classification. The emergence of Deep-learning techniques such as Convolutional-networks and RNN has resulted in a swift increase in correctness in certain picture categorization operations. In this work, a unique approach using LSTM is proposed to predict the gender of an individual by using many pre-trained transfer learning models. With the purpose of evaluate the effectiveness of this scheme, we conduct training on a Bi-LSTM model using an OU-ISIR-MVLP (Multi-view large population) Gait Dataset.
