The dataset comprises 10300 participants, balanced between males and females, and includes photos captured from 14 various viewing angles. Objectives to determine the age and gender of users. The top level of accuracy achieved by the suggested work in gender classification is 89%.

articleTitle: Sustainable Programming : A New Paradigm Shift Towards Sustainable Development
abstract: Technology is an indication of energy use, and specifically, the use of electricity plays a significant role in impacting the environment. As technology continues to advance, the importance of sustainability grows, ensuring that our innovations do not come at the cost of ecological balance. The research aims to discuss green computing and sustainability in data centers based on concepts involving application, facility, and sustainability measures. To solve these challenges, it is suggested that resolutions be made to accelerate the optimal algorithms, adopt an energy-saving language, and adhere to sustainable software development practices. In this context, programming languages are compared in terms of their power consumption, supported by graphics. The outcomes of the experiment demonstrate the potential for energy savings through efficient, sustainably implemented coding and confirm the importance of green software.

articleTitle: Detection of Unathorized Vechile in BRT Lane
abstract: The increasing number of unauthorized vehicles in the Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) lanes creates a significant challenge to urban transportation. Due to this efficiency and quality of safety decreases. Our project aims to develop an automated system that detects unauthorized vehicles that come into BRT lanes using deep learning techniques like YOLOv8. The system employs combination video surveillance, image processing, and deep learning models to accurately identify and track vehicles that violate the BRT regulations. The proposed solution enhances traffic management and reduces the incidence of unauthorized lane usage by integrating the real- time data processing and alert mechanisms. The system employs a dataset from Roboflow, extended with a self-made dataset containing images of various vehicles in BRT lanes. We utilize YOLOv8 for object detection to accurately identify and classify vehicles. Also, Easy-OCR is used to recognize text from license plates for validation and verification against authorized vehicle list. Our preliminary results demonstrate that the system achieves 80% accuracy in detecting unauthorized vehicles. Our solution is urban traffic management by reducing illegal lane usage and ensuring easier public transport operations.

articleTitle: Attention based Zero-Shot Learning for Unseen Class Classification
abstract: In the realm of computer vision and deep learning, recent strides have been made towards more robust image classification systems. However, traditional deep learning models encounter significant hurdles, including the demand for a large number of labeled data per category, the intricacy of distinguishing subtle differences between visually similar classes, and the failure to classify new classes. This study introduces a transformative approach to address these challenges: Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL). ZSL revolutionizes deep learning by training models to classify classes not present during training, employing attributes or semantic descriptions. This method seamlessly transfers knowledge from known to unknown categories by leveraging semantic cues or auxiliary data, eliminating the need for exhaustive labeled examples for every class used in analyzing the AWA2 and CUB datasets, standard benchmarks in the ZSL domain. The performance of the proposed model is analyzed using harmonic mean. The proposed model demonstrated significant improvements in generalization to unseen classes.

articleTitle: Unitary Camera Proximal Intensity Estimation using DEVIANT
abstract: Accurate depth estimation is crucial for applications like autonomous driving and augmented reality. This project proposes a novel approach to enhance monocular depth estimation (MDE) by integrating annotated and unannotated images. The methodology involves training a student model on a dataset combining labeled and pseudo-labeled data, leveraging a teacher model's knowledge trained on an extensive dataset. Data acquisition focuses on high-quality annotated datasets like KITTI and NuScenes. Preprocessing involves image resizing and normalization, with data augmentation techniques for diversity. Network architecture includes CNNs and ViTs for feature extraction, with FPNs for multi-scale feature representation. The project utilizes the DEVIANT model with the vanilla architecture for enhanced results, overcoming limitations of existing MiDAS architectures. Future scope includes applying the methodology to other vision tasks and incorporating more sophisticated network architectures. The propsed solution overcomes teh use of LIDAR and multi camera setups for such applications. Consequently, the proposed solution demonstrates outstanding zero-shot depth estimation capability, and also provides a promising foundation for subsequent tasks involving metric depth estimation and semantic segmentation.

articleTitle: Fake Image Detector using Machine Learning
abstract: The detection of fake images has become increasingly critical due to the proliferation of deepfakes and sophisticated image manipulation techniques used for misinformation, fraud, and public manipulation. This paper offers a thorough examination of various methods for detecting fake images, encompassing both traditional and contemporary strategies. Traditional techniques, including Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and Support Vector Machines (SVMs), focus on the analysis of statistical properties and the identification of inconsistencies in image features; however, these methods frequently encounter challenges with more subtle or complex alterations. In contrast, recent developments in the field harness deep learning methodologies, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), to significantly improve detection accuracy.CNNs excel in learning hierarchical features and detecting intricate patterns indicative of image tampering. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) also play a role in this domain by improving model robustness through adversarial training. Despite these advancements, challenges remain, including the evolving nature of manipulation techniques, the need for extensive annotated datasets, and computational demands. This review highlights the strengths and limitations of various methods and suggests future research directions to enhance fake image detection, such as multi-class classification, transfer learning, and real-time application optimizations.

articleTitle: Adaptive Traffic Control Using Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Urban congestion and transportation inefficiencies pose significant challenges that require innovative solutions. Traditional static traffic signal control methods struggle to adapt to dynamic traffic conditions, leading to delays and increased pollution. Adaptive Traffic Control using Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) represents a promising approach to enhance traffic signal systems' performance by dynamically adjusting signal timings based on real-time traffic patterns. This paper introduces an adaptive traffic signal controller that minimizes delays and effectively manages heavy traffic volumes. The controller optimizes signal phases for efficient traffic flow and reduced congestion by using DRL to learn from and enhance its decision-making process. The system's performance and adaptability are assessed using metrics such as average speed, queue length, Number of vehicles, and waiting time. Deep Q-Network-based algorithm is introduced, featuring a custom Q-function, which is developed and compared against existing algorithms in diverse scenarios. This comparison showcases the new algorithm's superior performance and effectiveness in addressing dynamic traffic situations. This study advances urban traffic management by introducing an intelligent and adaptable traffic signal controller. This innovation has the potential to significantly improve transportation system efficiency and urban mobility.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Emotion Classification
abstract: In this generation, social media platforms such as Twitter, Instagram and also e-commerce websites have become an integral part of our society. Social media is used for communication and it is also a platform where the users can express their thoughts and feelings. Also, users share their reviews on e-commerce websites. To analyze what exactly is the emotion of the user our machine learning models explores the sentiment analysis techniques for predicting emotions from the given text data. It follows a series of steps, starting with importing libraries, acquiring datasets, visualization, pre-processing, and model building. The data is used to train on a variety of models, including LSTM, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, and SVM. The performance of each model is evaluated using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Comparative analysis is conducted to determine the most effective model for emotion prediction. Furthermore, the research investigates emotion prediction for huge datasets and provides a procedure for exporting trained models for future usage. It provides insights into the performance of various machine learning algorithms in sentiment analysis, hence contributing to the understanding and interpreting emotions from textual data on various platforms.

articleTitle: Quantum Decryption using Shor’s Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents the generalized implementation of the quantum circuit utilized in Shor’s algorithm, which was simulated using the quantum simulator offered by IBM. Shor’s Algorithm is a ground-breaking Quantum Algorithm that works on Integer Factorization; for a classical computer, the following task would require an exponential amount of time, whereas a Quantum Computer running Shor’s Algorithm would only require Polynomial-time. Using the principles of Quantum Superposition and Quantum Entanglement, the algorithm demonstrates the potential of quantum computing to solve complex mathematical problems efficiently. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the implemented algorithm in Integer Factorization and discrete logarithm, disturbing the safety of major encryption algorithms. This paper contributes to advancing the understanding and practical application of quantum algorithms in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Memory-Efficient Neural Network Deployment Methodology for Low-RAM Microcontrollers Using Quantization and Layer-Wise Model Partitioning
abstract: This paper introduces a memory-efficient methodology for deploying neural networks (NNs) on low-RAM microcontrollers. The work utilizes a compact multilayer perceptron (MLP) with 50 neurons and 716 trainable parameters, achieving a classification accuracy of 97.22% on the MNIST-10 dataset. The trained MLP is split into separate, fully connected submodels to conserve RAM, each representing a specific layer. The submodels are sequentially executed in the order they appear in the original MLP, with only the active submodel in RAM at any given time, drastically reducing the RAM requirements. These submodels utilize the weights and biases of the pre-trained MLP, eliminating the need for additional training. Following this methodology, the trained model only requires a maximum of 1.3kB of RAM (along with the whole infrastructure) to process one MNIST image. In contrast, initially, the model parameters alone would have a cost 2.8 kB of RAM. The model parameters are integer quantized to save on flash memory and converted to floating-point during runtime with minimal accuracy loss. The RAM based execution also enables low-latency inference, primarily for batch processing tasks, and can be adapted to deploy a wider range of pretrained neural networks on low-RAM microcontrollers. A proofof-concept is demonstrated on an Atmega328p Arduino board with two kB RAM and 32 kB flash memory.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Smart Cervical Support System
abstract: In the last few decades, it has been observed that accidental patients are getting more severe injuries while handling the injured person due to spinal/neck injuries or not enough emergency support at the spot. Thus, we designed a portable device to support the human cranial and neural system in the neck region, which includes the top vertebral bones and major nerves. To avoid damaging the major nerve, emergency support staff must handle the unconscious individual with extreme caution after they have been hurt. If it is injured, the individual may experience compression, laceration, or contusion of the spinal cord, which may result in a coma, paralysis, or long-term repercussions on the neurological system. This article provides the solutions and discusses the challenges of implementing the GPS-based emergency cervical support system that is capable of activating an airbag in life-threatening circumstances. The system is developed with the help of various sensors and a digital controller. Explaining the design steps and the assembly arrangement will help the neck area be restrained and keep it as straight as possible. Hence, that saves the injured person from menacing injuries.

articleTitle: Verification of Harnessing Solar Energy in to Powertrain of Electric Small Commercial Vehicle through Bench Setup
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into the transportation sector, particularly in Electric Vehicles (EVs), holds promise for sustainable mobility and reduced carbon emissions. This paper explores the possible ways on how solar energy can be harnessed into the powertrain of Electric Small Commercial Vehicles (SCVs) to offset the load demands when vehicle is parked or in motion. An experimental bench setup has been developed to validate the test cases. The results of the experiments have been analyzed considering different practical factors which helps to anticipate the implications of solar integration in to vehicle.

articleTitle: EMGTTL: Transformers-Based Transfer Learning for Classification of ADL using Raw Surface EMG Signals
abstract: Surface Electromyography (sEMG) is widely studied for its applications in rehabilitation, prosthetics, robotic arm control, and human-machine interaction. However, classifying Activities of Daily Living (ADL) using sEMG signals often requires extensive feature extraction, which can be time-consuming and energy-intensive. The objective of this study is stated as follows. Given sEMG datasets, such as electromyography analysis of human activity databases (DB1 and DB4), with multi-channel signals corresponding to ADL, is it possible to determine the ADL categories without explicit feature extraction from sEMG signals. Further is it possible to learn across the datasets to improve the classification performances. A classification framework, named EMGTTL, is developed that uses transformers for classification of ADL and the performance is enhanced by cross-data transfer learning. The methodology is implemented on EMAHA-DB1 and EMAHA-DB4. Experiments have shown that the transformer architecture achieved 64.47% accuracy for DB1 and 68.82% for DB4. Further, using transfer learning, the accuracy improved to 66.75% for DB1 (pre-trained on DB4) and 71.04% for DB4 (pre-trained on DB1).

articleTitle: FLARE: Federated Learning And Resilient Encryption for Firewalls
abstract: Traditional firewalls rely on static rule-based mechanisms, where rules are manually defined and often written in specialized languages. While effective to a degree, these rules are inherently limited and can be easily bypassed by new and evolving types of malware, leading to significant security vulnerabilities. To address these challenges, we propose FLARE: Federated Learning And Resilient Encryption, a novel machine learning-based firewall solution. FLARE dynamically analyzes past network connections to predict and determine the appropriate actions for incoming traffic, thereby adapting to emerging threats in real-time.Given the sensitive nature of firewall data, which often contains confidential information, the training of machine learning models poses significant privacy risks. FLARE mitigates these risks by incorporating federated learning, allowing the model to learn from decentralized data sources without requiring raw data to be shared. To further enhance privacy, we introduce an encryption layer that ensures the central model learns from encrypted weights, preventing exposure of sensitive information known to the local model. This combined approach not only improves the resilience of firewalls but also safeguards the confidentiality of the data used in training, offering a robust solution for modern cybersecurity challenges.

articleTitle: Design Consideration of Table-top Model of an AI-Enabled Aquaponics System
abstract: Aquaponics is the fusion of hydro-farming with aquaculture, whereby vegetation produced in a soilless culture, typically in a regulated environment, uses the nutrients supplied by growing fish. Fish produce nearly all the nutrients needed for plant development. These systems may offer greater sustain-ability, lower resource use, and fewer environmental effects than traditional aquaculture. Most participants include education professionals, commercial operators, non-profit societies managing aquaponic systems as a hobby, and consultants selling products, materials, and services. Various operational conditions can influence these systems, such as the selection of species, restricted funding, and skewed market conditions. Owing to these problems, the farming sector is shifting toward automation or smart, which uses artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) to streamline processes and boost output. AI and IoT technology incorporate several cutting-edge methods and devices, such as big data, cloud computing, networking, sensor technology, and mobile applications. To keep this system’s popularity in mind, the study aims to design a tabletop model of an AI-enabled aquaponic system. This systematic approach uses scientific methodologies to produce study findings that can be disputed, improved, and repeated. This technique is anticipated to speed up the creation of useful systems, scientific knowledge, and smart commercial implementations. This research is essential for businesses as professionals planning to invest in new initiatives must consider manufacturing costs, product worth, and investment return.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease based on the State-Of-The-Art Deep Learning Approach
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a deep convolutional neural network architecture, code-named Inception, which sets a new benchmark for classification and detection tasks. Early detection of Alzheimer's disease (AD) is critical, as the brain is the primary organ affected, and early intervention can help slow disease progression. Traditionally, AD diagnosis relies heavily on MRI scans, a process that is both time-consuming and resource-intensive. However, recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) present promising solutions for more efficient detection. This study examines the application of various Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models for detecting AD in MRI images. A comprehensive comparison was performed on four distinct CNN architectures—Inception-V3, ResNet-152, VGG16, and VGG19—using MRI data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI). The images were categorized into four classes: Non-Demented, Very Mild Demented, Mild Demented, and Moderate Demented.While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) excel at identifying advanced dementia stages (Stages 5-7), accurately classifying the earliest, most elusive stages (Stages 2-4) remains a significant challenge. This paper tackles this crucial gap by systematically comparing various CNN models to achieve promising classification accuracy for these crucial early stages of dementia. Through rigorous analysis, we aim to advance the field of dementia detection by enabling earlier diagnosis and intervention, ultimately improving patient outcomes. Therefore, the application of machine learning technology can assist healthcare professionals in enhancing their efforts to combat Alzheimer's, a serious medical condition.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Early Dementia Detection Integrating Clinical Data and MRI Imaging
abstract: Dementia, particularly Alzheimer's disease, is a leading cause of cognitive decline, affecting millions globally. Early detection is vital for effective management, yet it remains challenging due to the complex nature of the disease. This paper explores the application of machine learning techniques to predict dementia, focusing on integrating clinical data and MRI images. We propose a hybrid model that combines Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to enhance prediction accuracy. The study addresses challenges such as data heterogeneity and model interpretability, highlighting the potential of multimodal approaches in dementia research. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining clinical and imaging data, offering insights into the future of personalized treatment for dementia.

articleTitle: A Dual-Model Solution for Business Reasoning with Large Language Models
abstract: Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have shown significant potential in automating tasks using natural language processing. However, as industry demands grow and generative AI advances, more complex tasks—such as intelligent reasoning, strategic decision-making, and business analysis—remain challenging for foundational models trained on general datasets. These tasks require domain-specific knowledge and a deeper contextual understanding, which current models struggle to provide. This research presents an approach that fine-tunes LLMs for specific business use cases by integrating domain knowledge and data analysis capabilities. Leveraging recent developments in structured query (SQL) based fine-tuned models and semantic search techniques, our methodology combines structured data retrieval from organizational sources with relevant domain expertise. This enables the model to answer complex analytical questions by connecting factual data from generated SQL queries to relevant business knowledge. We propose a dual-model system: a fine-tuned code-generating model for data extraction and a foundational model with visual reasoning capabilities. This combination ensures accurate alignment of data with the appropriate knowledge base, reducing the risk of hallucinated answers. The performance of our approach is compared against stand-alone fine-tuned models and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) models, demonstrating superior results in answering reasoning-based questions and supporting decision-making tasks. Overall, this research offers a systematic solution for integrating data-driven insights with business-specific knowledge, empowering leaders to make informed decisions based on accurate, visualized data and market-specific information.

articleTitle: Establish an Innovative ML-enabled Human Activity Recognition through Edge Computing
abstract: The use of a computer system to recognize human activity or gestures, Human Activity Recognition (HAR), enables real-time behaviour and emotion prediction in individuals. In the fields of ubiquitous edge computing (EC), human behaviour analysis, and human-computer interaction, HAR is a crucial area of research. Machine learning algorithms are used in various fields of research to identify both basic and complicated human activities. In this study, we proposed a novel Garra rufa fish-optimized multi-kernelized support vector machine (GRFO-MSVM) for the recognition of human activity. The suggested approach utilizes the EC’s capabilities to train a model, which is then applied to less potent edge devices for recognition. In this study, we collected a WISDM dataset for human activity. The pre-processed data are extracted using linear discriminate analysis (LDA) to reduce dimensionality in sensor data. The proposed method is implemented using Python software. The proposed method is compared to other existing algorithms. The study indicates the SVM can improve accuracy while performing HAR within the edge. The experimental result shows the SVM achieved better performance in accuracy (98.73%), precision (98.71%), recall (98.72%), and F1-score (98.8%).

Author Keywords: GarraRufa Fish Optimized Multi-Kernelized Support Vector Machine (GRFOMSVM)

articleTitle: Revolutionizing the Future of Automated Subjective Answer Sheet Evaluation System with Machine Learning and LLMs
abstract: Human evaluation of handwritten answer sheets is very inefficient, inaccurate, and potentially biased. This research work serves the purpose of addressing these drawbacks by developing an automated grading system that leverages advanced OCR technologies and machine learning algorithms. The system, utilizes Google Cloud Platform (Cloud Vision API) and Gemini 1.5 Pro for Optical Character Recognition, to process large capacity of answer sheets with variation in handwriting styles more accurately than the traditional methods. This leads to a significant increase in text extraction accuracy and grading reliability. Therefore, as comparison with the existing solutions demonstrates, the new system has an increased level of accuracy and efficiency, reducing human error and fairly assessing student performances. Thus, implementation of changes in traditional grading system may influence the feasibility of this work, giving educators the opportunity to engage more time in instructional activities.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Powered Forensic Evidence Storage: A New Approach to Data Security
abstract: The enforcement and protection of evidence do have a critical position in the judicial system and procedures. Traditional means of preserving evidence are susceptible to damage, loss, or unauthorized access, as they might be considered in today’s world. This paper provides a new means of keeping evidence-safe using blockchain technology, thus promoting safety, traceability, and authenticity. The proposed structure guarantees tamper-proof records and proper access to data with a decentralized and immutable ledger offered by the network. The cryptographic methodology coupled with smart contracts allows for the secure and transparent management of the lifecycle of forensic evidence. Analysis of the system architecture and its capability to transform the nature of evidence storage practice was done by this investigation. Notable improvements in data integrity, transparency, and operational efficiencies are evidenced when compared to traditional approaches via case studies and simulations. Pilot implementation study findings point to the strength, scalability, and effectiveness of blockchain in ensuring secure forensic evidence management. This work adds to the growing body of new literature on blockchain beyond cryptocurrency by demonstrating its capacity to tackle critical challenges facing forensic data security.

articleTitle: HIET: Height Images for Enhanced Terrain Perception for Robot Navigation
abstract: The representation of unknown environment poses a significant challenge in the field of robotics. The existing methods leverage elevation maps constructed from point cloud data from sensors like 3D-LiDAR or Stereo camera. Robots utilizes this map for navigating through environments and achieving perceptual locomotion control. In this paper, we introduce a grid based elevation mapping pipeline which harnesses the height information from 3D point cloud to generate a 2D height image as intermediate format and use to create 2.5D elevation map. The proposed height image based approach is a new way of getting elevation map and is equally holds relevance due to its ability to process lower-dimensional data while still constructing a 2.5D map. To achieve this, we first find the receptive field of image by establishing the correspondence between image pixels and 3D points through projection. In the receptive field of the image, the pixel intensities are computed by checking the average height of points resulting in an image with height intensities. Further, this height image is post-processed as a gridmap layer to have structured and informative representation. Our pipeline is specifically engineered to achieve good processing speed and it is highly configurable to allow user to configure the map parameters and enable a wide variety of environment representation. We carried out extensive testing on four open source data namely LioSAM, Rellis3D and Fast_LIO. We also showcase its practical applicability by deploying across multiple robotic platforms with diverse configurations. The proposed pipeline includes a ROS2 interface for easy integration with any Autonomous Navigation System (ANS) stack.

articleTitle: Product Detection Analytics on Instagram Videos
abstract: Object detection has become a cornerstone of computer vision, with applications spanning from autonomous vehicles to surveillance systems. This paper presents a novel approach using YOLOv8 for real-time object detection in video streams, coupled with a method to calculate the total duration of detected objects. We demonstrate the system's effectiveness using a custom dataset, highlighting its potential for various real-world applications where object presence duration is crucial. Our results show the count and duration of the object, indicating the viability of this approach for industrial use by various Brands to know about the appearance of their products.

articleTitle: RouteMate - RideSharing Application
abstract: RouteMate is a ride-sharing application that offers safe, secure, and affordable rides at almost half the price compared to other popular ride-sharing application. Developed using Kotlin, Firebase, and Android Studio, RouteMate aims to revolutionize urban commuting experiences. With two primary functionalities, users can choose to either become drivers or request rides. Drivers input their starting and ending locations, and the application uploads their requests to the server. When a rider with a matching route is found, they receive a notification to share the ride. Payment is processed through RouteMate, and the journey is continuously monitored by the application’s servers. Similarly, riders can request rides by entering their locations and selecting from a list of available drivers. Payments are securely processed via Razorpay, and rides commence immediately. The application enables both drivers and riders to connect seamlessly, facilitating cost-effective and convenient transportation solutions. During the journey, users can raise SOS requests if needed, and after completion, they can submit ratings about the ride. RouteMate ensures the safety of its users through a strict, precise, and exacting verification process, offering legal authentication for every customer. The uniqueness of RouteMate lies in its flexibility, allowing users to be both drivers and riders, and offering rides at significantly reduced prices. Moreover, drivers have the opportunity to earn part-time income through the application, further enhancing its application in urban commuting landscapes.

articleTitle: The Common Rust Detection in Corn by Utilization of Hybrid Deep Learning Algorithm VGG-16
abstract: The Common Rust (CR) is a disorder in corn plantations which is caused due to the fungus Puccinia sorghi, common rust in corn is characterized by the small, reddish-brown pustules that develop on the leaves, and often start forming in the rows. These pustules developed on the leaves, with time turn black, with the yellowing surrounding tissue, potentially reducing the crop yield. Common rust in the corn plantation reduces photosynthesis, leading to the stunted growth and lower yields. Severe infections can cause the premature leaf death, the weakened plants, and increased vulnerability to other diseases and environmental stressors. Common rust in corn thrives in the cool and moist conditions, leading to the increased fungicide use, soil contamination, and potential water pollution. The reduced yields may also drive land expansion, contributing to the deforestation and habitat loss. This work introduces a deep-learning classifier designed to differentiate between two main types of image data, the corn leaves affected by common rust disease and healthy corn leaves. The images undergo de-noising to improve quality. The cleaned data is then used to train VGG-16 algorithm based model, and it achieves high accuracy. In summary, this research aims to develop a highly accurate image classifier for detecting common rust disease in corn, and it achieves an accuracy rate of 99.47%.

articleTitle: Transforming Industrial Operations through Industry 4.0’s Integration of Emerging Solutions
abstract: The Industry 4.0 revolution seeks to transform manufacturing and industrial operations through advanced technologies, including the Internet of Things (IoT), Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, Blockchain, Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), 3D Printing, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), Robotics, Computer Vision (CV), Natural Language Processing (NLP), and 5G Technology. This convergence of technologies is giving birth to smart factories that allow real-time data exchange and autonomous decision-making. Eventually, such changes will enable organizations to gain considerable productivity growth, enhanced flexibility, and responsiveness to market demands. This paper outlines how such technologies are changing the production processes through increased transparency and automation throughout the supply chains of various industrial sectors. It also pays attention to the socio-economic changes that digital transformation has on workers and gives a sense of how industries handle complicated issues while trying to remain competitive and sustainable in an ever-changing economic environment.

articleTitle: Integrated Deep Learning Model for Predictive Diagnosis of Life-Threatening Disease Condition
abstract: The degree of complexities associated with medical data has been always a rising concern among the healthcare sectors due to manifold valid reasons. Review of existing studies showcases usage of learning-based approaches being dominant towards solving diagnosis related issues of Life-Threatening Diseases or condition of patient during their hospital stay and yet characterized by various loopholes. Therefore, the proposed study addresses this problem by presenting a simplified and yet innovative integrated learning-based scheme towards leveraging predictive diagnosis performance on larger and complex medical dataset of patients in intensive care units. The scheme presents a Convolution Neural Network (CNN) based scheme integrated with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) with attention layer to find 54% increased predictive accuracy and 82% of faster response time in contrast to related method.

articleTitle: Enhancing Nucleus and Cytoplasm Segmentation in Cervical Cytology Using Deep Learning
abstract: Cervical cancer, with over 660,000 cases in 2022, ranks as the fourth most frequent malignancy in women globally, with low- and middle-income nations accounting for approximately 94% of the 350,000 annual deaths. The challenging diagnosis of cervical cancer, often detected at advanced stages, has been addressed by recent advancements in high-throughput quantitative imaging of 2D cell cultures. Image segmentation automates the traditionally manual process of Pap smear cell diagnosis. While conventional approaches are effective, they face limitations in underrepresented cellular regions, noise, and blurriness in microscopy. Semantic segmentation causes inter-class competition, which causes performance issues for popular segmentation algorithms such as U-Net and Mask R-CNN in multi-class contexts. Our novel approach addresses these challenges by treating nucleus and cytoplasm segmentation as separate tasks, significantly enhancing overall segmentation performance. The nucleus, characterized by higher density and darker appearance, presents a more readily learnable target for the U-Net algorithm. While watershed and similar methods partially mitigate the issue of overlapping and occluded cells, challenges persist. A viable approach is to use pre-trained open-source models like Cellpose, which have been trained on thousands of images. Fine tuning these models through transfer learning for cytoplasm segmentation has produced remarkable outcomes. Pairing segmented nuclei and cytoplasm via centroid distance analysis enhances segmentation accuracy and resolves cellular overlaps. With an accuracy of 99.3%, an IoU of 83.91%, a Dice Coefficient of 91.04%, and precision of 89.88% for nucleus segmentation, and 98.81%, 95.62%, and 91.81% for cytoplasm segmentation, our method demonstrated remarkable accuracy across several parameters. These findings show how our method may help with cervical cancer diagnosis and detection.

articleTitle: Distributed Ledger Based Optimal Solution Architecture for A Secure Blood Screening System
abstract: Managing blood screening data is critical for healthcare, requiring secure and transparent systems to safeguard public health. Existing methods often lack secure access to donors' medical histories, posing risks. Hyperledger Fabric, a distributed ledger technology, offers a robust solution for managing health data securely. This paper proposes a decentralized blood screening system using Hyperledger Fabric to record transactions, donor, and recipient data, employing chaincode for eligibility checks. Its modular architecture ensures privacy, integrity, and immutability. The study explores how Hyperledger Fabric's architecture meets blood screening requirements, focusing on optimizing latency, throughput, and block space utilization through customized configurations. Experiments with Hyperledger Fabric v2.5 assessed performance by adjusting endorsement strategies and block sizes. The results, analyzed for performance differences, provide recommendations for tuning configuration factors like batch timeout and maximum message count. The Hyperledger Caliper tool was used to measure transaction throughput and latency, leading to optimized blockchain architecture for blood screening. Findings indicate that customized blockchain configurations can significantly enhance performance metrics crucial for real-time healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Smart Defense: Machine Learning-Based Web Application Firewall
abstract: The rise in internet usage has been revolutionary, as nearly 8 billion people in the world in 2024—5.35 billion of them, or around 66% of the world's population, are active internet users. These statistics clearly show that the development of web applications has skyrocketed as they offer accessibility and flexibility, but it also introduces serious threats that can inflict considerable damage on these applications and systems and compromise the personal information of their users. Hence, leveraging security mechanisms is equally crucial. In this research, an abnormality-based web application firewall model was developed using machine learning-based classification algorithms, mainly XG Boost. The performance of different classification-based algorithms was evaluated by developing different models. The proposed model achieves higher performance in differentiating between normal and malicious requests. As per investigation, our proposed model serves to be effective in differentiating between normal and malicious requests by delivering an accuracy level of 94.2%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Agricultural Practices with AgroDialogue: A Chatbot Framework
abstract: The agriculture sector faces significant challenges due to the limited adoption of efficient practices by farmers, leading to reduced crop yields and quality. This research introduces a specialized chatbot tailored for agricultural inquiries, leveraging advanced technologies such as Large Language Models integrated with Knowledge Graphs and vector databases. The chatbot performs thorough query analysis and delivers personalized information, facilitated by a user-friendly interface that supports seamless interaction, effective query categorization, and clear responses. Additionally, it incorporates voice functionality to improve accessibility for users with learning disabilities or literacy challenges. Unlike existing solutions, this chatbot is uniquely designed for agriculture, offering free, portable, and reliable guidance on farming techniques and related topics. By empowering farmers to make informed decisions about crop selection, pest management, and irrigation methods, the system aims to promote sustainable farming practices and enhance financial outcomes. The research methodology includes data preparation, model selection, and the implementation of a knowledge graph memory base. The development of APIs and databases ensures effective communication and user engagement, with comprehensive testing validating the system’s functionality, performance, and accuracy in diverse scenarios. This paper highlights the potential of advanced technologies in creating specialized agricultural chatbots, providing a promising approach to disseminate agricultural knowledge and support stakeholders in the sector.

articleTitle: A Survey on Artificial Intelligence based Photovoltaic Cell Defect Detection Techniques
abstract: With the increase in demand for solar energy in the form of photovoltaic (PV) panels have become an important component in sustainable energy applications. The visible defects (cracks, black spots, corrosion, etc.) in PV cells can occur during manufacturing times or while sustaining under external environmental conditions like rain, extreme temperature, humidity, etc. As a result, timely fault analysis in solar panels is essential in order to enhance both the lifespan and energy efficiency performance. The Electrolumince (EL) imaging technique is one of the popular technique used to scan PV modules in order to identify these critical defects like cracks. However, traditional PV fault detection methods rely on manual inspection and hence tedious, prone to human errors. This survey paper discusses the different methodologies and techniques using artificial intelligence (AI), Deep learning (DL), and Computer vision (CV) for quick, reliable, and efficient crack detection in PV panels using EL imaging analysis. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Residual Neural Networks (ResNet), and Visual Geometry Group (VGG) have demonstrated significant improvements in defect detection accuracy. This survey paper also discusses the standard datasets available in this domain and a comparative analysis of proposed techniques in the literature.

articleTitle: Improving Asset Information Management in the Oil & Gas Sector: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Effective asset information management is essential in the oil and gas sector to support optimised decision-making, particularly in managing complex surface engineering processes. The technical demands of oilfield construction management affect the growth and utilisation rates of engineering resources, yet current data management systems face challenges such as high data acquisition costs, limited data sharing, and weak analytical capabilities. This paper addresses these gaps by proposing a core data management system powered by machine learning (ML) techniques to enhance data acquisition, sharing, and intelligent analysis. Using the publicly available 3W database from Petrobras, evaluated multiple ML models, including KNN, LSTM networks, Federated Learning (FL), DT, RF, and RNN, assessing performance on metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1score. KNN with SMOTE achieved superior results, with 99.36% accuracy, 99.10% precision, 99.37% recall, and a 99.64% F1 score, effectively distinguishing normal from undesirable events. Our findings highlight the need for more advanced, real-time analytics in oilfield asset management, and future research will focus on deep learning architectures and expanding datasets with real-world data to further improve operational insights.

articleTitle: A Vocal Features-Based Predictive Model for Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis
abstract: This study looks at how audio metrics extracted from speech samples might be used to diagnose Parkinson's disease (PD) using machine learning (ML) techniques. The set contains various acoustic characteristics, including frequency variations, jitter, shimmer and other specific measurements of voice, rather than actual voice recordings. Through rigorous preprocessing and comprehensive exploratory data analysis, the data set was carefully prepared for model training. Many ML methods, including k-nearest neighbour, decision tree, logistic regression, Bayes naves, support vector machines (SVM), have been evaluated and implemented. Ensemble methods, such as voting classification methods, were used to exploit the collective power of several models. It is particularly remarkable that a random forest classifier with the entropy criterion achieved an impressive accuracy rate of about 97.3% on the test set. In addition, LLAMA's integration into the language model interface facilitates real-time prediction and enhanced result interpretation. This integration enables users to rapidly assess the likelihood of PD based on acoustic properties, promoting the development of effective diagnostic tools for clinical and broader applications.

articleTitle: Secured Encrypted Morse Code Communication using Fernet in Defense Applications
abstract: In today's digital age, ensuring the security and confidentiality of voice communication is crucial. This research work presents an innovative approach that leverages a combination of speech recognition, Morse code conversion, and encryption techniques to achieve secure transmission of spoken messages. By integrating these methods, this research provides a system for encoding, encrypting, and securely transmitting voice data, ensuring that sensitive information remains protected throughout the communication process. This article explains a multi-step process that combines speech recognition, Morse code conversion, and encryption to securely send spoken information. The workflow begins with Speech-to-Text Conversion, where spoken words are converted into text using advanced speech recognition technology. The text is then transformed into Morse Code for further processing. To ensure the confidentiality of the message, the Morse code is encrypted using Fernet symmetric encryption. This encrypted Morse code can be securely transmitted or stored. Upon receiving the encrypted message, the process is reversed: Morse Code Decryption returns the encrypted Morse code to its original form, which is then converted back into text through Morse Code to Text Conversion. Finally, the text is transformed back into Spoken Words using text-to-speech technology, completing the secure transmission of the original spoken message. This research combines classic communication techniques with modern encryption methods to create a system for secure and encrypted voice communication.

articleTitle: Decentralized Credential Verification System
abstract: Blockchain and the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) are two decentralized technologies poised to revolutionize data storage, management, and sharing. Blockchain is a distributed ledger technology offering secure, transparent record-keeping and reduced transaction costs. IPFS is a decentralized file storage system designed to mitigate issues like censorship and data loss, using content addressing for improved speed and reliability. Integrating blockchain and IPFS can create powerful systems, such as decentralized marketplaces for file storage and sharing. This integration can eliminate intermediaries, enhance transparency, and bolster security. This paper explores the potential of these technologies, their individual strengths, and their combined impact on creating more secure, transparent, and efficient data management systems, benefiting individuals, organizations, and society.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Recognition Using Attention-Based CNN Algorithm
abstract: Skin cancer is a common and potentially lethal condition, requiring precise and effective diagnosis techniques. This research introduces a sophisticated method for skin cancer detection with an attention-enhanced convolutional neural network (CNN) model, emphasizing the Xception algorithm. The proposed method emphasizes attention mechanisms inside the CNN to preferentially concentrate on critical lesion regions, hence strengthening feature extraction and augmenting classification accuracy. The system is assessed using the HAM10000 dataset, demonstrating strong performance across seven categories of skin lesions. A comparative examination with conventional CNN models indicates that attention-based CNNs, particularly Xception, achieve markedly superior accuracy, precision, and recall, underscoring its promise in clinical diagnosis. This method improves early detection of skin cancer and offers a promising pathway for enhancing patient outcomes via dependable, automated diagnosis.

articleTitle: Enhancing DM/OTA/FOTA Systems Architecture for IOT using Collaborative Computing Paradigms Reference Architecture
abstract: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has heightened the need for efficient and reliable Over-The-Air (OTA) and Firmware Over-The-Air (FOTA) systems for effective Device Management (DM). Our literature review revealed that most research primarily focuses on trust, security, and the delivery of software updates, with little or no emphasis on developing a complete architectural framework. This paper proposes an enhanced architecture for DM/OTA/FOTA, that leverages Collaborative Computing Paradigms (CCP) to optimize DM, OTA and FOTA processes in dynamic IoT environments. By integrating a unified resource pooling strategy, and dynamic distribution of data processing our architecture enhances operations. We explore the fluidity of computing across Edge, Fog, and Cloud paradigms, facilitating seamless firmware updates while ensuring scalability and extendability. Through real-world use cases, including automotive telematics, smart buildings and data center monitoring systems, we demonstrate the versatility and effectiveness of the proposed enhancement using the CCP-IOT-RA model of DM, OTA and FOTA systems. This work lays the groundwork for future research and applications in collaborative IoT architectures.

articleTitle: Sensitive Security: The Next Generation Alarm System
abstract: This paper describes a low-cost security system for investigating the removal of an external object, for example, a watch or chain of a probe. When the object is disconnected, the circuit switch on an LED light for the purpose of telling the user visually that something is amiss and a buzzer to give an audible signal that something is wrong. This circuit is run by a 9-V battery and is equipped with a 555 timer integrated circuit and a BC547 transistor. The 555 timer IC is connected in monostable mode where control timing is changed via the P1 port. The BC547 transistor acts as a switch to control the output devices since its versatility enables its use in different security systems. Also, this design is an economic way of preventing theft and safeguarding items belonging to an individual. The paper also presents the description of the circuit and detailed characteristics of the system along with the experimental results pointing to the effectiveness and possible cost realization of the system.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Biomarkers for Alzheimer’s disease
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease is gradually losing the cognitive ability and memory functions necessary to meet the challenges of daily life and causes severe disability in affected individuals. It has been known that with a close study of potential environmental and lifestyle risk factors for Alzheimer's, the specific modifiable risk factors of Alzheimer's can be obtained. Exposure to air pollution and heavy metal toxicity leads to oxidative stress and inflammation, which further promotes neuronal damage. In these lifestyle factors, problems in terms of sedentary lifestyle, inappropriate diet, chronic stress might disturb cellular metabolism, in addition to promoting amyloid-beta deposition. Social isolation and disturbances in sleep exacerbate the decline in cognitive function. It links psychosocial factors to the pathogenesis of this disease. Elucidation of these influences may enhance the preventive strategies and identify the potential intervention points along with biomarker-based diagnostics toward more effective management of Alzheimer's disease. As the number one cause of dementia in the world it way affects millions of people all over the world. The disease is marked by the presence of amyloid-beta plaques and tau protein tangles in the brain that disrupts normal processes and leads to nerve cell death. Alzheimer’s disease is the outcome of genetic susceptibility coupled with environmental factors and life style. The major genes linked with this ailment include the APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2 genes and any APOE ε4 allele. There are more recent risk variants that have been reported recently. The vast majority of the known risk variants for AD are connected to the established functions of APP, PSEN1, and APOE ε4; however, there is evidence that recent discoveries of risk variants in other genes, such as the TREM2 gene influencing immune response and amyloid processing, or BIN1, linked to tau pathology, are evidence of new areas of influence. Epigenetic mechanisms from DNA methylation to histone modification and non-coding RNAs are rapidly emerging areas of research that point out how factors of environment and lifestyle can influence gene expression without changing the sequence of the DNA. Thus, these findings suggest critical interactions between genes and their environment, which might eventually lead to novel therapeutic targets and biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease. This disease starts with minimal signs of neurocognitive dysfunction and maybe followed by severe dementia. At the time of writing this paper there is no known cure for Alzheimer’s disease. Hence, the management plans for AD mainly focus on reducing the signs and the progression of the disease by using medication and palliative care. New developments in management of Alzheimer's include new pharmacological interventions, like aducanumab, which are anti-amyloid antibodies that aim to reduce amyloid plaques, and non-pharmacological interventions: cognitive stimulation therapy or music therapy, which has proven to enhance quality of life. Lifestyle interventions related to diet and exercises are part of the care plan for the patient themselves to complement medical treatments and better a patient's well-being. Current developments associated with discovery of new and more specific biomarkers, imaging techniques, in addition to expanded knowledge on the disease pathology signify hope for the early detection of this disease and increased accuracy in treatment plans. Resume of the current knowledge of Alzheimer’s disease is also offered and the need for further investigations on aetiology factors, diagnostic technique and treatment strategies for improved management of the disorder is also stressed.

articleTitle: Optimizing Pathfinding in Dynamic Environments: A Comparative Study of A* and D-Lite Algorithms
abstract: This is one of the most important challenges in domains like robotics, AI, and video games: given some start point, there generally needs to be a minimum cost way found to reach a specified goal. Algorithms like A would not change the static conditions since they compute extremely efficiently when the environments are static. But for dynamic environments, with all the new challenges of moving obstacles and changing terrains besides others, do increase the complexity. We compare to a quite heuristically well-known A* against an incremental search algorithm which we call D-Lite. Our ability is to deal with dynamic environments ubiquitously. In simulation, we demonstrate how though A* is highly suited for static environments, D-Lite best competes in dynamic scenarios owing to its ability to incrementally adapt to changing conditions without calculating paths anew from scratch. This explains why real-time applications are perfect for optimum pathfinding. It also throws much light on how D-Lite in dynamic algorithms adapts to environments for optimum operations.

articleTitle: Temporal Energy Consumption Exploration and Time Series Forecasting of Electricity Dynamics
abstract: In recent times, the judicious management of energy resources has emerged as a paramount concern owing to the escalating global energy demand. Studying and predicting energy consumption patterns plays an important role for effective demand side management, providing the optimal allocation of energy resources, and promoting sustainability. This research fulfills the gap by providing a study of temporal consumption patterns. The essential aim is to use forecasting techniques for predicting household electricity usage on an hourly basis, in contrast to the actual energy production metrics from the power houses in India. The study is performed on the energy consumption dataset from city of Seaux, France, adding hourly electricity usage and readings from various residents over a time period. To deepen this understanding of the dynamics of demand and supply by the energy industry, it is complemented by parallel analysis on actual production data from Indian power stations. Against the backdrop of many intricate time-lagged relationships in the energy sector, state-of-the-art multivariate time series forecasting (MTSF), Prophet and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, approaches have been applied and found useful in interpreting complex temporal correlations present within energy production and consumption data. The hybrid models Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN- Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU)), CNN-LSTM, Stacked GRU and Stacked LSTM, LSTM Dense, GRU Dense has been implemented. The comparative analysis is carried out to know the advantages and disadvantages of the applied forecasting models. The GRU Dense Model emerged as the most accurate, achieving an impressive Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.03%. The research findings bring out the complexity of temporal patterns of energy use, bringing out those key variables that affect electricity demand and supply.

articleTitle: Robust Person Identification and Tracking in High-Exposure Environments Using YOLOv7
abstract: The identification and detection of individuals in well-lit environments, such as university hallways, pose distinct challenges stemming from fluctuations in shadows, luminosity, and contrast. In this investigation, we devised and assessed a system for person identification and tracking utilizing the YOLOv7 model applied to a tailored dataset of images collected in brightly illuminated college corridors. The principal aim was to attain a high level of accuracy in individual detection and subsequently establish a resilient person tracking framework. Our methodological approach encompassed a comparative analysis of two techniques—contrast stretching and adaptive histogram equalization—to enhance image quality and augment detection efficacy. The YOLOv7 model, trained on the COCO dataset, constituted the foundational framework for object detection. The findings revealed a remarkable detection accuracy of 99.7%, with adaptive histogram equalization exhibiting superior performance in addressing discrepancies in shadows, brightness, and contrast.

articleTitle: Predictive Analytics of Cardiovascular Disease Using Machine Learning
abstract: It is estimated that cardiovascular disease (CVD) is responsible for almost 18 million fatalities around the world, making it the top cause of mortality even today. When it comes to reducing death, rates caused by cardiovascular disease, early detection and accurate risk assessment are absolutely necessary. Currently available advancements in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) have the potential to significantly improve the accuracy of both the prediction and diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases. This in-depth analysis investigates the use of a variety of machine learning and deep learning approaches in the field of predictive analytics for cardiovascular disease (CVD). These techniques include decision trees, support vector machines, random forests, neural networks, and convolutional neural networks. These techniques show promise in terms of improving diagnosis accuracy and making it possible to implement interventions that are more effective, which will ultimately contribute to the global effort to reduce the burden of cardiovascular disease.

articleTitle: Integrating Deep Embedded Clustering with DeepLabV3 for Effective Camouflaged Object Detection
abstract: Camouflaged Object Detection (COD) poses a significant challenge in computer vision due to the minimal contrast between the object and its surroundings. Conventional methods often struggle in such scenarios. This study introduces an approach by integrating DeepLabV3, a cutting-edge semantic segmentation model, with Deep Embedded Clustering (DEC) to enhance COD. From DeepLabV3, the ResNet101 model is fine-tuned to achieve precise segmentation. Then DEC is applied to help with unsupervised feature learning that enables the model to differentiate elusive differences between camouflaged objects and their backgrounds. The proposed method's efficiency is inveterated on the ACOD10K dataset. It shows distinct improvements in quantitative metrics and qualitative evaluations with a Mean Square Error (MSE) of 0.337 compared to other methods. This approach establishes a robust foundation by integrating DEC into deep learning frameworks to tackle the complexities of COD.

articleTitle: Advancing Subsea Reservoir Management through Digital Twin
abstract: When designing an intricate system, it's crucial to apply system concepts, principles, and rules to gain a comprehensive understanding of the challenge at hand. The subsea system's architecture refers to the organization of a system, including its components, relationships with the environment, and structure defined by elements, interfaces, processes, restrictions, and behaviors. One of its components, a reservoir, is an underground deposit that is intended to hold hydrocarbons such as oil or gas for extraction. Additionally, digital twin (DT) technology allows for extensive monitoring, analysis, and optimization of assets and processes in a variety of industries, including construction, engineering, architecture, and subsea maintenance. Overall, this paper presents an approach to using Autodesk Maya software to create a digital twin (DT) of the reservoir, which is a vital part of subsea systems.

articleTitle: Role of Artificial Intelligence for Noninvasive Height Measurement Applications: A Survey
abstract: Height measurement is crucial across various domains including healthcare, ergonomics, security, and forensic analysis. Traditional methods, such as stadiometers, often require cooperation from the subject and can be intrusive, posing significant challenges especially with children, the elderly, or individuals with disabilities. This survey paper addresses the growing need for artificial intelligence (AI) based noninvasive, automated height measurement techniques that can effectively estimate height without physical interaction. In this paper, we examined different state of the art methodologies for height measurement application area, including AI, computer vision (CV), deep learning (DL), depth imaging, and 3D laser scanning. While 3D scanning and depth imaging methodologies provide precise measurements, but they require specialized equipments which leads to additional costs for implementation. Recently, DL and advanced CV models have shown great accuracy in height estimation. Promising solutions for uncooperative subjects can be found by utilizing facial recognition and anatomical traits, and incorporating biometric parameters which can improve prediction accuracy. Despite these advancements, challenges remain with methods requiring multiple images or additional equipment, underscoring the need for more practical and user-friendly solutions. This survey highlights the necessity for tailored approaches to address specific measurement challenges and proposes guidelines for future studies to improve efficiency of noninvasive height estimation technologies.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Hand Radiographic based Person Authentication
abstract: One of the most important components of the majority of computer vision automation systems is human authentication. It is impossible for conventional systems that are based on fingerprints, iris, face, and palm prints to identify a human being when these exterior biometric elements are destroyed due to things like rashes, wounds, severe burns, and other similar factors. The most important characteristics of any person authentication system are its security, resilience, privacy, and non-forgery capabilities. A comprehensive overview of numerous methods of person authentication based on hand radiographs is presented in this work. The technique, radiographic modality employed, dataset, benefits, and downsides of these methods are some of the topics that are discussed. It fills in the study gaps that were discovered during the survey and throws up the door to the possibility of future improvements to the authenticity of individuals based on radiography. Additionally the effectiveness of the system is analyzed for the different machine learning algorithms such as support vector machine (SVM), K-nearest neighbor (KNN), classification tree (CT) and random forest (RF).

articleTitle: Application of NLU based Sentiment Analysis in the Hybrid Stock Price Forecasting Model using Deep Learning Model
abstract: For any developing market, like the Indian stock market, creating a stock market forecasting model is difficult. The reason being investor behavior on economic factors like changes in the western stock market, variations in the price of commodities on the international market, war-related escalations, and central bank actions influence the stock prices in emerging stock markets and less work on prior studies to consider investor behaviors based on several economic elements that affect price movement. To address this issue, a hybrid forecasting model is developed that uses Deep Learning algorithms through a multivariate Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model to predict future open and close prices by combining sentiment analysis data of economic information along with historical prices. The findings indicate that sentiment analysis data on economic information has an impact on stock price movement. The proposed model achieved better results in terms of coefficient for the determinant (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) for the predicted result. The study findings can be used in future studies of other markets and asset classes where investor opinion toward certain events may have an impact on price fluctuations.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Conservation in WSN
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are the fastestgrowing technology for many application services. Weather monitoring, traffic forecasts, reconnaissance, and academic research are included. Security measures are the best test for wireless communication system issues since sensor nodes are scattered in remote areas. An energy-efficient technique of the Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy (LEACH) called the Stable Election Protocol (SEP) extends the lifespan of heterogeneous wireless sensor networks. Energy inequality reduces performance and longevity regardless of the situation. Adding node vitality to cluster head selection reduces cluster head energy consumption; using interim nodes reduces cluster node energy consumption. Heterogeneous-aware SEP extends the stable period before the first node passes. Certain applications require consistent sensor input, hence this protocol is needed. Each node's weighted election choice probability to become cluster head determines SEP success. The results show that the Proposed Efficient (PE-SEP) SEP methodology changes energy utilization to increase longevity dramatically. Compare the LEACH and SEP protocols with the upgraded SEP algorithm and the proposed SEP (PE-SEP) algorithm in MATLAB R2021a.

articleTitle: A Reference Architecture Based on Collaborative Computing Paradigms Adopted for Dynamic IoT Systems
abstract: Current IoT architecture standards offer a foundational reference model for building diverse applications. However, they lack detailed provisions for emergent aspects such as various paradigms of computing, data processing, and dynamism of the system. Addressing these limitations, the IoT architecture based on Collaborative Computing Paradigms (CCP) presents unique characteristics, including, (a) Interconnection and interplay (b) Dynamic distribution of data processing (c) Fluidity of computing across paradigms (d) Storage and data management across participating paradigms (e) Scalability and extendability of the architecture. Reference Architectures (RA) are foundational reference models, and provide a blueprint for creating applications in a broad set of applications and applications domains. A CCP-IOT-RA is an architecture which overcomes the challenges of dynamic IoT environments, and is a reference architecture that satisfies the requirements of a RA. An architecture based on CCP-IOT-RA was designed, and developed for dynamic IoT environments. The developed architecture was evaluated against the requirements of RA and dynamic IoT environments using real-world applications. With this, it is validated that the designed CCP-IOT-RA indeed is a reference architecture that can be applied across various application domains.

articleTitle: Rhythmic Pattern Recognition - A Review
abstract: Rhythmic pattern recognition is crucial in music analysis and information retrieval, involving the identification and classification of rhythmic structures. This paper offers a detailed overview of advanced methods in rhythmic pattern recognition, including time-domain, frequency-domain, and symbolic representations. We examine various machine learning techniques, such as statistical models, neural networks, and deep learning. Additionally, we address the challenges and limitations of current methods and propose directions for future research. Understanding rhythmic patterns is vital for performing, composing and analysing music.

articleTitle: Quantum Secure Email Communication for Phishing Prevention
abstract: The rise of sophisticated phishing attacks has necessitated stronger security measures for email communication, especially in sensitive environments. This paper proposes a Quantum Secure Email Communication Framework designed to prevent phishing by integrating Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) with traditional email security mechanisms. The framework leverages quantum keys to encrypt email communication, ensuring that only legitimate users with the correct quantum key can send and receive secure emails. The architecture also incorporates a Phishing Detection Engine that validates email content and sender information using quantum-encrypted keys, alerting users to potential phishing threats. The system operates through the secure exchange of quantum keys between the sender’s email server and the user via a QKD Channel, with quantum encryption applied to secure outgoing and incoming emails. In parallel, the phishing detection module analyses all email traffic for signs of malicious activity, using a QKD-based Email Validator to confirm the legitimacy of emails. This hybrid approach ensures both the privacy of communication and the proactive detection of phishing attempts, offering a robust defense mechanism in the increasingly hostile landscape of digital communication.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fertility Detection Accuracy Through Machine Learning: A Comprehensive Analysis and Novel Approaches
abstract: This paper provides a unique method that uses machine learning approaches to improve the accuracy of fertility identification in cotton crop management. The study emphasizes how crucial precise soil fertility forecasting is to maximizing productivity, making the most use of available resources, and promoting sustainable agriculture. Though useful, traditional methods frequently have drawbacks like labor intensity, spatial unpredictability, and time consumption. The study investigates the integration of sophisticated algorithms—such as Support Vector Machines, Random Forests, and Naive Bayes—with information from IoT devices, remote sensing, and past crop performance in order to address these issues. The study shows how machine learning models may lower expenses, automate data collecting, and increase forecast accuracy through a thorough investigation. Significant gains in memory, F1 scores, and precision are shown by the experimental results, offering a solid foundation for data-driven agricultural decision-making. The results imply that integrating machine learning with fertility detection can result in more productive and scalable farming methods, which would eventually improve crop yields and resource management.

articleTitle: Grocery Purchase through Blockchain System
abstract: The integration of blockchain technology into the grocery purchasing process offers a transformative approach to enhancing transparency, security, and efficiency. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for a blockchain-based grocery system, detailing each step from user registration and identity verification to product listing, smart contract creation, and real-time inventory management. Consumers can place orders with confidence, knowing that payments are securely processed and supply chain logistics are fully transparent. The use of IoT devices ensures quality control during transportation, while smart contracts automate delivery and receipt confirmation. Additionally, the system supports consumer feedback and dispute resolution through immutable records and predefined arbitration mechanisms. This innovative application of blockchain technology aims to revolutionize the grocery sector, fostering trust and accountability among all stakeholders involved. Future research will explore the potential for AI integration and address scalability and interoperability challenges.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Electoral Integrity With A CNN-Powered Smart Voting System Using Advanced Facial Recognition Techniques
abstract: A Smart Voting System is a sophisticated web service that offers a straightforward and secure way to conduct elections using blockchain technology. It guarantees the accuracy of votes, even in real-time voting, with fraud nearly eliminated, making the electoral process more straightforward and democratic. This research proposed CNN (convolutional neural network) algorithms, which provide a secure and easy-to-use face recognition-based user interface. The system compares a facial scan with data stored on central servers and confirms your identity if a match is found. The system uses the acronym UDD(Universal Democratic Delivery) to represent a voter’s ability to vote on e-Enabled days, DDM(Direct Democracy Machine) and DRE(Direct Recording Electronic) machines, dead-end checking with removable inking pins, discounted absentee ballots, and more. The paper thoroughly discusses the claimed 99.5% accuracy of the CNN algorithm and explores the potential for private information leakage if implemented directly on user devices. This approach enables a more democratic process to emerge, ensuring that elections are both authentic and convenient. The experimental results demonstrated higher accuracy than traditional methods.

articleTitle: Indigenously Designed and Development of Actively Q-Switched Nanosecond Nd:YAG Laser
abstract: The design, development, and characterization of an actively Q-switched Nd:YAG laser system with high peak power is presented in this paper. Establishing the design characteristics and validation of indigenously developed pulsed Nd:YAG laser along with its flashlamp electrical power supply system is the main goal of this research. To optimize the laser’s major parameters—the optical resonator design, flashlamp pumping, and Q-switching mechanism—theoretical analysis and simulations are carried out. The modelling results guided the experimental development by offering important insights into the predicted performance characteristics of the laser system with relatively higher extraction efficiency, pulse-to-pulse stability as well as high optical-to-optical efficiency. For the laser system to operate effectively and dependably, the laser cavity design along with the pulse-forming network, trigger circuit, and simmer circuit of the flashlamp power supply, have to be carefully designed and implemented. The demonstration of a high peak power actively Q-switched Nd:YAG laser oscillator with a repetition rate of 10 Hz, pulse width of 30 nanosecond with maximum pulse energy of 130 mJ is successfully achieved. The Nd:YAG laser system’s fruitful development and characterization described in this paper, together with the electrical system’s native design can be used to design and build indigenous electrical power supply for both flashlamp pumped as well as diode pumped Nd:YAG laser systems and maximizing the optimization of its functionality.

articleTitle: Standardised Schema and Taxonomy for AI Incident Databases in Critical Digital Infrastructure
abstract: The rapid deployment of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in critical digital infrastructure introduces significant risks, necessitating a robust framework for systematically collecting AI incident data to prevent future incidents. Existing databases lack the granularity as well as the standardized structure required for consistent data collection and analysis, impeding effective incident management. This work proposes a standardized schema and taxonomy for AI incident databases, addressing these challenges by enabling detailed and structured documentation of AI incidents across sectors. Key contributions include developing a unified schema, introducing new fields such as incident severity, causes, and harms caused, and proposing a taxonomy for classifying AI incidents in critical digital infrastructure. The proposed solution facilitates more effective incident data collection and analysis, thus supporting evidence-based policymaking, enhancing industry safety measures, and promoting transparency. This work lays the foundation for a coordinated global response to AI incidents, ensuring trust, safety, and accountability in using AI across regions.

articleTitle: 5G Campus Network Deployment for Outdoor-to-Indoor Rescue Use Cases
abstract: The advent of 5G private networks enables diverse communication demands including emergency response services such as forest and people rescue. These campus networks can meet specific operational and security demands of stakeholders. Due to the sophistication of network deployment and application integration, this paper explains these procedures showcasing firefighting mission requisites. The development includes the hardware and software of network components, the integration of 5G components, and the integration of Internet of Things devices with the network. The deployment has been preceded by a radio planning that assists finding the optimal location and orientation for the sector antenna in rescue context. The network deployment has been assessed by radio, throughput, and latency measurements to examine the network coverage quality, performance and reliability, respectively. The paper summarizes the challenges of outdoor-to-indoor propagation and proposes future solutions based on the state-of-the-art in the technology.

articleTitle: Disaster Prediction Using Appropriate Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This paper provides the insights of disaster forecasting methods, focusing on the strengths, limitations, and applications of other models and ideas to predicting natural disasters. Disasters and pandemics are most unlikely events which concerns many nations. Till date multiple ways are used to detect or predict natural disasters. Various machine learning techniques are used in detecting, preventing or mitigating disasters. We focus on predicting natural disasters beforehand to reduce its effects using XGBoost algorithm. The study shows the challenges of accurate forecasting and early warning systems.The paper also highlights about user friendly and interactive integrated website for disaster prediction. The paper gives the overview of the successful development and implementation of various models to predict earthquake, tsunami, flood and landslide.
